```{r chunk-2 }
# generic cache: compute an object and save it to disk, or reload if already saved
# use for any expensive computation (ml fits, simulations, etc.)
fit_or_load <- function(path, refit, fit_fun) {
  if (refit || !file.exists(path)) {
    obj <- fit_fun()
    saveRDS(obj, path)
    obj
  } else {
    readRDS(path)
  }
}

# helper: standardize itsadug prediction outputs across versions
tidy_itsadug_predictions <- function(pred_df, xvar = "norm_mid", keep = NULL) {
  pred_df <- as_tibble(pred_df)

  fit_col <- intersect(c("fit", "pred", "estimate", "est"), names(pred_df))[1]
  ci_col  <- intersect(c("CI", "ci", "SE", "se", "se.fit"), names(pred_df))[1]

  if (is.na(fit_col)) {
    stop("No fitted-value column found in the itsadug output.")
  }

  out <- pred_df %>%
    rename(.fitted = all_of(fit_col))

  if (!is.na(ci_col)) {
    out <- out %>%
      mutate(.lower_ci = .fitted - .data[[ci_col]],
             .upper_ci = .fitted + .data[[ci_col]])
  }

  if (!is.null(keep)) {
    out <- out %>%
      select(any_of(c(xvar, keep, ".fitted", ".lower_ci", ".upper_ci")))
  }

  out
}

# helper: get response-scale predictions from itsadug, one curve at a time.
# xvar names the swept predictor so the same helper serves trajectory and lag plots.
get_itsadug_curve <- function(model, cond, keep = NULL,
                              xvar = "norm_mid",
                              transform_fun = plogis) {
  pred_raw <- get_predictions(model,
                              cond          = cond,
                              rm.ranef      = TRUE,
                              sim.ci        = TRUE,
                              print.summary = FALSE)

  pred_df <- tidy_itsadug_predictions(pred_raw, xvar = xvar, keep = keep)

  pred_df %>%
    mutate(.fitted   = transform_fun(.fitted),
           .lower_ci = transform_fun(.lower_ci),
           .upper_ci = transform_fun(.upper_ci))
}

# helper: significant segments for difference plots.
# y_sig is placed at the global minimum across all panels so that the segment
# sits at a consistent height in faceted figures.
get_sig_segments <- function(diff_df) {
  global_y_min <- min(diff_df$difference - diff_df$CI)
  global_y_max <- max(diff_df$difference + diff_df$CI)
  global_y_sig <- global_y_min - 0.1 * (global_y_max - global_y_min)

  diff_df %>%
    mutate(sig = (difference - CI) > 0 | (difference + CI) < 0) %>%
    group_by(deliberation_function) %>%
    mutate(block = cumsum(sig != lag(sig, default = first(sig)))) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    filter(sig) %>%
    group_by(deliberation_function, block) %>%
    summarise(x    = min(norm_mid),
              xend = max(norm_mid),
              .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(y_sig = global_y_sig)
}


# Report the saved model estimates and tests, with separate columns for b and edf.
tbl_gam <- function(
  model, caption = NULL, exponentiate = FALSE, var_labels = NULL,
  level_labels = NULL, digits = 2, pvalue_digits = 3, fit_stats = TRUE,
  show_formula = FALSE, section_headers = TRUE, estimate_label = NULL,
  output = c("flextable", "data"), additional_effects = NULL
) {
  stopifnot(inherits(model, "gam"))
  output <- match.arg(output)
  fam <- stats::family(model)
  smry <- summary(model) # One summary, including mgcv's special RE tests.
  if (identical(exponentiate, "auto"))
    exponentiate <- identical(fam$family, "binomial") && identical(fam$link, "logit")
  stopifnot(is.logical(exponentiate), length(exponentiate) == 1L)
  if (is.null(estimate_label)) estimate_label <- if (exponentiate) "OR" else "b"
  vl <- c(score_01 = "Score", active = "Activation", confidence_01 = "Confidence",
          response_confidence = "Confidence", deliberation_function = "Function",
          response = "Accuracy", subject_id = "Participant", question = "Item",
          trial_id = "Trial", chunk_id = "Chunk", norm_mid = "Relative time",
          log_n_chunks = "Log number of chunks",
          lag_conf_chunk_dev_1 = "Previous confidence (within trial)",
          lag_conf_chunk_dev_2 = "Confidence two chunks earlier (within trial)",
          conf_trial_dev = "Confidence (trial deviation)",
          conf_subject_mean = "Confidence (participant mean)",
          lag_active_1 = "Previous activation", lag_active_2 = "Activation two chunks earlier",
          lag_score_01_1 = "Previous intensity", lag_score_01_2 = "Intensity two chunks earlier",
          lag_confidence_1 = "Previous confidence", lag_confidence_2 = "Confidence two chunks earlier",
          lag_confidence_1_z = "Previous confidence (standardized)",
          lag_confidence_2_z = "Confidence two chunks earlier (standardized)")
  for (f in c("control", "generation", "justification", "regulation")) {
    label <- tools::toTitleCase(f)
    vl[paste0("lag_", f, "_chunk_dev_1")] <- paste0("Previous ", f, " (within trial)")
    vl[paste0("lag_", f, "_chunk_dev_2")] <- paste0(label, " two chunks earlier (within trial)")
    vl[paste0(f, "_trial_dev")] <- paste0(label, " (trial deviation)")
    vl[paste0(f, "_subject_mean")] <- paste0(label, " (participant mean)")
    for (lag in 1:2) vl[paste0("lag_",f,"_",lag)] <- paste0("Previous ",f," (n−",lag,")")
  }
  if (length(var_labels)) vl[names(var_labels)] <- gsub("Prior", "Previous", unname(var_labels), fixed=TRUE)
  pv <- function(v) if (v %in% names(vl)) unname(vl[v]) else v
  pl <- function(v,l) {
    if (!is.null(level_labels[[v]]) && l %in% names(level_labels[[v]]))
      return(unname(level_labels[[v]][l]))
    if (v == "response" && l == "Incorrect") return("Biased")
    l
  }
  xl <- model$xlevels
  # Reference labels are valid only for treatment-coded fixed factors.
  treatment <- names(xl)[vapply(names(xl),function(v) {
    ct <- model$contrasts[[v]]
    is.character(ct) && identical(ct,"contr.treatment")
  }, logical(1))]
  refs <- setNames(vapply(treatment, function(v) pl(v,xl[[v]][1]),character(1)),treatment)
  split_factor <- function(term) {
    for (v in names(xl)[order(-nchar(names(xl)))]) {
      if (startsWith(term,v)) {
        l <- substring(term,nchar(v)+1)
        if (l %in% xl[[v]]) return(list(var=v,level=l))
      }
    }
    list(var=term,level=NA_character_)
  }
  pp <- function(term) {
    if (term == "(Intercept)") return("Intercept")
    parts <- strsplit(term,":",fixed=TRUE)[[1]]
    labs <- vapply(parts,function(part) {
      z <- split_factor(part)
      if (is.na(z$level)) return(pv(z$var))
      if (!(z$var %in% treatment)) return(paste(pv(z$var),pl(z$var,z$level)))
      if (length(parts)>1 && z$var == "deliberation_function") return(pl(z$var,z$level))
      if (z$var == "deliberation_function") return(paste0(pl(z$var,z$level)," vs. ",refs[z$var]))
      if (z$var == "lag_active_1") return("Previous activation (active vs. inactive)")
      paste0(pl(z$var,z$level)," vs. ",refs[z$var])
    },character(1))
    paste(labs,collapse=" × ")
  }
  smooth_by_label <- setNames(model$smooth,vapply(model$smooth,`[[`,character(1),"label"))
  ps <- function(term) {
    sm <- smooth_by_label[[term]]
    if (inherits(sm,"random.effect")) {
      vars <- sm$term
      fac <- vapply(vars,function(v) is.factor(model$model[[v]]),logical(1))
      if (all(fac)) return(paste0("Random intercept: ",paste(vapply(vars,pv,character(1)),collapse=" × ")))
      return(paste0("Random slope: ",paste(vapply(vars[!fac],pv,character(1)),collapse=" × "),
                    " by ",paste(vapply(vars[fac],pv,character(1)),collapse=" × ")))
    }
    base <- paste(vapply(sm$term,pv,character(1)),collapse=" × ")
    if (identical(sm$by,"NA")) return(base)
    v <- sm$by; lev <- sm$by.level
    if (startsWith(v,"interaction(")) {
      vars <- trimws(strsplit(sub("^interaction\\((.*)\\)$","\\1",v),",",fixed=TRUE)[[1]])
      # Construct full level combinations; do not split levels at periods.
      combos <- expand.grid(lapply(vars,function(x) levels(model$model[[x]])),stringsAsFactors=FALSE)
      k <- match(lev,apply(combos,1,paste,collapse="."))
      if (!is.na(k)) lev <- paste(mapply(pl,vars,as.character(combos[k,]),USE.NAMES=FALSE),collapse=" × ")
    } else lev <- pl(v,lev)
    paste0(base,": ",lev)
  }
  pt <- as.data.frame(smry$p.table)
  stat_type <- if (grepl("^t",names(pt)[3])) "t" else "z"
  critical <- if (stat_type == "t") stats::qt(.975,smry$residual.df) else stats::qnorm(.975)
  param <- data.frame(term=rownames(pt),label=vapply(rownames(pt),pp,character(1)),
                      estimate=pt[[1]],SE=pt[[2]],low=pt[[1]]-critical*pt[[2]],
                      high=pt[[1]]+critical*pt[[2]],statistic=pt[[3]],p=pt[[4]],
                      statistic_type=stat_type,row.names=NULL)
  st <- as.data.frame(smry$s.table)
  smooth <- data.frame(term=rownames(st),label=vapply(rownames(st),ps,character(1)),
                       edf=st[[1]],ref_df=st[[2]],statistic=st[[3]],p=st[[4]],
                       statistic_type=names(st)[3],row.names=NULL)
  smooth$random <- vapply(smooth$term,function(t) inherits(smooth_by_label[[t]],"random.effect"),logical(1))
  mm <- model$model
  fit <- c("Model rows"=nrow(mm))
  if (all(c("subject_id","question","norm_mid") %in% names(mm)))
    fit["Chunks"] <- nrow(unique(mm[c("subject_id","question","norm_mid")]))
  for (v in intersect(c("subject_id","question"),names(mm)))
    fit[paste0(pv(v),"s")] <- length(unique(mm[[v]]))
  if (all(c("subject_id","question") %in% names(mm))) fit["Trials"] <- nrow(unique(mm[c("subject_id","question")]))
  fit <- c(fit,"Deviance explained (%)"=smry$dev.expl*100)
  if (grepl("^Beta",fam$family) && is.function(fam$getTheta)) fit["Beta precision"] <- fam$getTheta(TRUE)
  meta <- list(family=fam$family,link=fam$link,method=model$method,refs=refs,
               formula=paste(deparse(stats::formula(model),width.cutoff=500),collapse=" "),
               parametric_statistic=stat_type,smooth_statistic=names(st)[3],
               residual_df=smry$residual.df,exponentiate=exponentiate,
               fit=fit,ci_distribution=if(stat_type=="t") "t" else "normal")
  result <- list(parametric=param,smooth=smooth,meta=meta,additional_effects=additional_effects)
  if (output == "data") return(result)
  format_gam_table(result, caption=caption, digits=digits, pvalue_digits=pvalue_digits,
                   fit_stats=fit_stats, show_formula=show_formula,
                   section_headers=section_headers, estimate_label=estimate_label)
}

# Keep the table layout separate so formatting changes do not require refitting.
format_gam_table <- function(result, caption=NULL, digits=2, pvalue_digits=3,
                             fit_stats=TRUE, show_formula=FALSE,
                             section_headers=TRUE, estimate_label=NULL) {
  param <- result$parametric; smooth <- result$smooth; meta <- result$meta
  exponentiate <- meta$exponentiate
  if(is.null(estimate_label)) estimate_label <- if(exponentiate) "OR" else "b"
  fmt <- function(x) {
    x[abs(x)<0.5*10^(-digits)] <- 0
    formatC(x,format="f",digits=digits)
  }
  fp <- function(x) vapply(x,function(p) {
    if(is.na(p)) return("")
    if(p<.001) return("< .001")
    sub("^0\\.",".",formatC(p,format="f",digits=pvalue_digits))
  },character(1))
  test <- function(type,x) paste(if(type=="Chi.sq") "χ²" else type, "=", fmt(x))
  keys <- c("Term","b","SE","CI","edf","ref_df","Test","p")
  rows <- list(); kinds <- character()
  add <- function(x,kind="value") {
    rows[[length(rows)+1L]] <<- setNames(as.character(x),keys)
    kinds <<- c(kinds,kind)
  }
  group <- function(label) if(section_headers) add(c(label,rep("",7)),"section")
  group("Parametric coefficients")
  est <- if(exponentiate) exp(param$estimate) else param$estimate
  lo <- if(exponentiate) exp(param$low) else param$low
  hi <- if(exponentiate) exp(param$high) else param$high
  for(i in seq_len(nrow(param))) add(c(param$label[i],fmt(est[i]),fmt(param$SE[i]),
    paste0("[",fmt(lo[i]),", ",fmt(hi[i]),"]"),"","",
    test(param$statistic_type[i],param$statistic[i]),fp(param$p[i])))
  for(re in c(FALSE,TRUE)) {
    z <- smooth[smooth$random==re,,drop=FALSE]
    if(!nrow(z)) next
    group(if(re) "Random effects" else "Smooth terms")
    for(i in seq_len(nrow(z))) add(c(z$label[i],"","","",fmt(z$edf[i]),fmt(z$ref_df[i]),
      test(z$statistic_type[i],z$statistic[i]),fp(z$p[i])))
  }
  panel_rows <- list()
  for(panel in result$additional_effects) {
    start <- length(rows)+1L
    group(panel$title)
    z <- panel$data
    for(i in seq_len(nrow(z))) add(c(z$label[i],fmt(z$estimate[i]),fmt(z$SE[i]),
      paste0("[",fmt(z$low[i]),", ",fmt(z$high[i]),"]"),"","",
      test(z$statistic_type[i],z$statistic[i]),fp(z$p_adjusted[i])))
    panel_rows[[length(panel_rows)+1L]] <- start:(length(rows)-1L)
  }
  if(fit_stats) {
    group("Sample and model fit")
    f <- meta$fit
    count <- function(name) formatC(f[name],format="d",big.mark=",")
    sample <- paste0("N = ",count("Chunks")," chunks",
      if(f["Model rows"]!=f["Chunks"]) paste0(" (",count("Model rows")," observations)") else "",
      "; ",count("Trials")," trials; ",count("Participants")," participants; ",count("Items")," items.")
    add(c(sample,rep("",7)),"fit")
    add(c(paste0("Deviance explained = ",formatC(f["Deviance explained (%)"],format="f",digits=1),"%."),rep("",7)),"fit")
  }
  display <- as.data.frame(do.call(rbind,rows),stringsAsFactors=FALSE)
  ft <- flextable::flextable(display,col_keys=keys)
  ft <- flextable::set_header_labels(ft,Term="Term",b=estimate_label,
    SE=if(exponentiate) "SE (link)" else "SE",CI="95% CI",edf="edf",ref_df="Ref. df",Test="Statistic",p="p")
  ft <- flextable::border_remove(ft)
  ft <- flextable::font(ft,fontname="Times New Roman",part="all")
  ft <- flextable::fontsize(ft,size=9.5,part="all")
  ft <- flextable::padding(ft,padding=2,part="all")
  ft <- flextable::height_all(ft,height=15/72,part="all")
  ft <- flextable::align(ft,j=1,align="left",part="all")
  ft <- flextable::align(ft,j=2:8,align="center",part="all")
  ft <- flextable::valign(ft,valign="center",part="all")
  ft <- flextable::width(ft,j=keys,width=c(2.13,.42,.42,1.04,.52,.52,.75,.50))
  ft <- flextable::italic(ft,j=c("b","SE","edf","p"),part="header")
  for(i in which(kinds=="section")) {
    ft <- flextable::merge_at(ft,i=i,j=1:8,part="body")
    ft <- flextable::bold(ft,i=i,part="body")
  }
  for(i in which(kinds=="fit")) {
    ft <- flextable::merge_at(ft,i=i,j=1:8,part="body")
    ft <- flextable::align(ft,i=i,j=1,align="left",part="body")
  }
  rule <- officer::fp_border(color="black",width=.75)
  ft <- flextable::hline_top(ft,border=rule,part="header")
  ft <- flextable::hline_bottom(ft,border=rule,part="header")
  ft <- flextable::hline_bottom(ft,border=rule,part="body")
  ft <- flextable::set_table_properties(ft,layout="fixed",opts_word=list(split=FALSE,keep_with_next=FALSE))
  ft <- flextable::keep_with_next(ft,i=which(kinds=="section"),value=TRUE,part="body")
  for(i in panel_rows) ft <- flextable::keep_with_next(ft,i=i,value=TRUE,part="body")
  # Keep random effects and the short summary panels together on long tables.
  tail_start <- which(kinds=="section" & display$Term=="Random effects")
  if(length(tail_start) && nrow(display)>tail_start)
    ft <- flextable::keep_with_next(ft,i=tail_start:(nrow(display)-1L),value=TRUE,part="body")
  # Keep the small sample-summary block on one page.
  frows <- which(kinds=="fit")
  if(length(frows)>1) ft <- flextable::keep_with_next(ft,i=head(frows,-1),value=TRUE,part="body")
  if(show_formula) ft <- flextable::add_footer_lines(ft,values=meta$formula)
  if(!is.null(caption)) ft <- flextable::set_caption(ft,caption)
  attr(ft,"gamm_report") <- result
  attr(ft,"gamm_row_kinds") <- kinds
  ft
}
```

```{r chunk-3 }
# lag-1 residual autocorrelation for a fitted gam/bam.
# pooled ACF: residuals concatenated across series with NA separators at
# boundaries so cross-series pairs don't contribute to lag-k counts.
# this is the least biased summary with short series and matches the convention
# bam() uses internally when rho is estimated.
#
# heuristic: |ACF1| > 0.2 is worth a closer look
check_autocorr <- function(model, series_vars,
                           max_lag = 4,
                           problematic_threshold = 0.2) {
  model_name <- deparse(substitute(model))

  mdf <- as.data.frame(model$model)
  mdf$.resid <- residuals(model)
  mdf$.sid   <- interaction(mdf[, series_vars, drop = FALSE], drop = TRUE)

  # total series and how many are long enough to contribute a lag-1 pair
  series_lengths <- mdf %>% count(.sid, name = "len")
  n_series_total <- nrow(series_lengths)
  n_series_used  <- sum(series_lengths$len >= 2)

  # pooled: insert NAs between series, then one acf() over the lot
  pooled <- mdf %>%
    arrange(.sid) %>%
    group_by(.sid) %>%
    group_modify(~ tibble(r = c(.x$.resid, NA_real_))) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    pull(r)

  acf_pooled <- stats::acf(pooled, lag.max = max_lag,
                           plot = FALSE, na.action = na.pass)
  lag1_pooled <- acf_pooled$acf[2, 1, 1]

  tibble(
    model          = model_name,
    n_series       = n_series_total,
    n_series_used  = n_series_used,
    lag1_pooled    = lag1_pooled,
    problematic    = abs(lag1_pooled) > problematic_threshold
  )
}
```

## Data

We load the scored chunks, rename the LLM-scored columns to a consistent prefix, keep only Reflect / Lure trials from unfamiliar participants, drop single-chunk responses, and compute normalized within-question time.

```{r chunk-4 }
# all otherwise eligible chunks, before applying the minimum-chunk criterion
chunks_scored_eligible <- read.csv("./Output/scored_chunks.csv") %>%
  rename(response_control = control_mean,
         response_generation = generation_mean,
         response_justification = justification_mean,
         response_regulation = regulation_mean,
         response_confidence = confidence_mean,
         response_repetition = repetition_mean,
         response_answer_selection = answer_selection_mean) %>%
  filter(response %in% c("Reflect", "Lure"),
         familiar == 0) %>%
  mutate(response = if_else(response == "Reflect",
                            "Correct",
                            "Incorrect"))

# dataset restricted to trials initially containing at least two chunks
chunks_scored <- chunks_scored_eligible %>%
  group_by(subject_id, question) %>%
  filter(n_distinct(chunk_id) > 1) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(trial_id = factor(interaction(subject_id, question, drop = TRUE)),
         n_words_chunk = str_count(str_squish(chunk_text), "\\S+")) %>%
  group_by(subject_id, question) %>%
  mutate(question_start = min(start_time, na.rm = TRUE),
         question_end = max(end_time, na.rm = TRUE),
         question_duration = question_end - question_start,
         norm_start = (start_time - question_start) / question_duration,
         norm_end = (end_time - question_start) / question_duration,
         norm_mid = ((start_time + end_time) / 2 - question_start) / question_duration,
         chunk_duration = end_time - start_time,
         n_words = sum(n_words_chunk, na.rm = TRUE),
         question_duration_tot = max(end_time)) %>%
  ungroup()

# column names for the seven scored functions and matching display labels
score_cols <- c("response_control", "response_generation", "response_justification",
                "response_regulation", "response_confidence", "response_repetition",
                "response_answer_selection")

score_labels <- c(
  response_control          = "Control",
  response_generation       = "Generation",
  response_justification    = "Justification",
  response_regulation       = "Regulation",
  response_confidence       = "Confidence",
  response_repetition       = "Repetition",
  response_answer_selection = "Answer Selection"
)

# the four core functions used in the trajectory models
core_cols <- c("response_control", "response_generation",
               "response_justification", "response_regulation")

core_labels <- c(
  response_control       = "Control",
  response_generation    = "Generation",
  response_justification = "Justification",
  response_regulation    = "Regulation"
)
```

## Validation with hand-scored data

We correlate the LLM scores with two hand-coded binary indicators: whether the participant reconsidered their initial response, and whether they verbalized reasons. 

```{r chunk-6 }
# trial-level averages of the LLM scores, kept alongside the hand-scored flags
avg_scores <- chunks_scored %>%
  group_by(subject_id, question) %>%

    control = mean(response_control, na.rm = TRUE),
    generation = mean(response_generation, na.rm = TRUE),

    regulation = mean(response_regulation, na.rm = TRUE),
    confidence = mean(response_confidence, na.rm = TRUE),
    repetition = mean(response_repetition, na.rm = TRUE),
    answer_selection = mean(response_answer_selection, na.rm = TRUE),

cor_cross <- cor_all$r[llm_vars, hand_vars]

)

  unname(llm_var_labs[llm_vars]),
  unname(hand_var_labs[hand_vars])
)

dimnames(p_cross) <- dimnames(cor_cross)

p_corr_validation <- ggcorrplot(
  cor_cross,
  p.mat = p_cross,
  insig = "blank",

  lab_size = 4,
  colors = c("darkblue", "white", "darkred"),

# default confidence intervals from psych::corr.test()
psych_cor <- psych::corr.test(
  select(avg_scores, all_of(c(llm_vars, hand_vars))),
  method = "spearman",
  adjust = "none"
)

# default confidence intervals from psych::corr.test()
cor_validation_table <- expand_grid(
  llm_var = llm_vars,
  hand_var = hand_vars
) %>%
  mutate(result = map2(llm_var, hand_var, function(x, y) {
    ct <- psych::corr.test(
      as.numeric(avg_scores[[x]]),
      as.numeric(avg_scores[[y]]),
      method = "spearman",
      adjust = "none"
    )

    tibble(rho = unname(ct$r)[1],
           lower = ct$ci$lower[1],
           upper = ct$ci$upper[1],
           p_value = unname(ct$p)[1])
  })) %>%
  unnest(result) %>%
  mutate(LLM_measure = unname(llm_var_labs[llm_var]),
         Hand_scored_measure = unname(hand_var_labs[hand_var]),
         `Spearman's rho [95% CI]` = sprintf("%.2f [%.2f, %.2f]",
                                             rho,
                                             lower,
                                             upper),
         p = if_else(p_value < .001,
                     "< .001",
                     sub("^0", "", sprintf("%.3f", p_value)))) %>%
  select(LLM_measure,
         Hand_scored_measure,
         `Spearman's rho [95% CI]`,
         p)

cor_validation_table %>%
  kable(col.names = c("LLM measure",
                      "Hand-scored measure",
                      "Spearman's rho [95% CI]",
                      "p"),
        caption = paste0(
          "Spearman correlations between trial-level LLM scores and ",
          "hand-scored indicators."
        ))
```

This result further validates our LLM-scoring pipeline


## Preparing data for GAMM fitting

### Removing chunks dominated by repetition and answer selection

We start with a simple beta GAMM on Repetition and Answer Selection over normalized time, to confirm that these functions dominate at the edges of each verbalization.

```{r chunk-7 }
# avoid exact 0 / 1 for the beta family
eps <- 0.001

# long format for the two functions of interest, with rescaled scores
chunks_rep_ans <- chunks_scored %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols      = c("response_repetition", "response_answer_selection"),
    names_to  = "deliberation_function",
    values_to = "score"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    deliberation_function = recode(deliberation_function,
                                   response_repetition       = "Repetition",
                                   response_answer_selection = "Answer Selection"),
    deliberation_function = factor(deliberation_function),
    subject_id = factor(subject_id),
    question   = factor(question),
    score_01   = pmax(eps, pmin(1 - eps, score / 100))
  )

# refit switch for this GAMM
refit_gam_beta_rep_ans <- FALSE

gam_beta_rep_ans <- fit_or_load(
  path  = "./Output/Saved_models/gam_beta_rep_ans.rds",
  refit = refit_gam_beta_rep_ans,
  fit_fun = function() {
    gam(
      score_01 ~ deliberation_function +
        s(norm_mid, by = deliberation_function, k = 10) +
        s(subject_id, bs = "re") +
        s(question,   bs = "re"),
      family = betar(link = "logit"),
      data   = chunks_rep_ans,
      method = "REML"
    )
  }
)

tbl_gam(gam_beta_rep_ans)
```

From the plot above, we can define "edges" as chunks in the first or last 20% of normalized time. The question is whether Repetition and Answer Selection dominate these segments in a way that would bias the trajectories of the four core functions.

```{r chunk-10 }
# tag each chunk as Start / Middle / End
chunks_edge <- chunks_scored %>%
  mutate(position = case_when(
    norm_mid < 0.2 ~ "Start",
    norm_mid > 0.8 ~ "End",
    TRUE           ~ "Middle"
  ))

# six functions relevant at the edges (confidence is dropped here)
edge_cols <- c(core_cols, "response_repetition", "response_answer_selection")
edge_labels <- c(core_labels,
                 response_repetition       = "Repetition",
                 response_answer_selection = "Answer Selection")

# long format for those six functions
chunks_edge_long <- chunks_edge %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols      = all_of(edge_cols),
    names_to  = "deliberation_function",
    values_to = "score"
  ) %>%
  mutate(deliberation_function = recode(deliberation_function, !!!edge_labels))

# mean score per function × position
edge_summary <- chunks_edge_long %>%
  group_by(position, deliberation_function) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_score = mean(score, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_score   = sd(score,   na.rm = TRUE),
    n = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(position = factor(position, levels = c("Start", "Middle", "End")))

p_edge_scores <- ggplot(edge_summary,
                        aes(x = deliberation_function, y = mean_score, fill = position)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(0.8), width = 0.7, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = mean_score - sd_score / sqrt(n),
                    ymax = mean_score + sd_score / sqrt(n)),
                position = position_dodge(0.8), width = 0.25) +
  labs(x = "Deliberation function", y = "Mean score (± SE)", fill = "Position") +
  jtools::theme_apa() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1))

p_edge_scores

ggsave("./Output/Preprocessing/edge_middle_function_scores.svg",
       plot = p_edge_scores, dpi = 600,
       width = fig_size_wide[["width"]], height = fig_size_wide[["height"]])
```

For each chunk, we identify the highest-scoring function among the six (four core + Repetition + Answer Selection). This tells us how often Repetition or Answer Selection "wins" at the edges.

```{r chunk-11 }
# per-chunk dominant function, across the six edge-relevant ones
chunks_dominant_all <- chunks_edge %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = all_of(edge_cols), names_to = "func", values_to = "val") %>%
  mutate(func = recode(func, !!!edge_labels)) %>%
  group_by(subject_id, question, chunk_id, position) %>%
  slice_max(val, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  rename(dominant_function = func, dominant_score = val)

# share of chunks where each function dominates, by position
dominance_counts <- chunks_dominant_all %>%
  count(position, dominant_function) %>%
  group_by(position) %>%
  mutate(pct = round(n / sum(n) * 100, 1)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(position = factor(position, levels = c("Start", "Middle", "End")))

p_dominance <- ggplot(dominance_counts,
                      aes(x = dominant_function, y = pct, fill = position)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(0.8), width = 0.7, alpha = 0.8) +
  labs(x = "Dominant function", y = "% of chunks", fill = "Position") +
  jtools::theme_apa() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1))

p_dominance

ggsave("./Output/Preprocessing/dominant_function_by_position.svg",
       plot = p_dominance, dpi = 600,
       width = fig_size_wide[["width"]], height = fig_size_wide[["height"]])
```

At the edges (norm_mid < 0.20 or > 0.80), some chunks are almost entirely captured by Repetition (re-reading the question) or Answer Selection (stating a final answer). We flag a chunk as dominated when the top-scoring non-core function accounts for more than 60% of the total chunk score across the six functions, and remove those chunks before fitting the trajectory models so that the GAMMs capture the core reasoning process.

```{r chunk-12 }
# only repetition and answer selection count as edge-contaminating
non_core_edge <- c("Repetition", "Answer Selection")

# per-chunk stats at the edges: which function dominates and by how much
chunk_stats <- chunks_edge %>%
  filter(position != "Middle") %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = all_of(edge_cols), names_to = "func", values_to = "val") %>%
  mutate(func = recode(func, !!!edge_labels)) %>%
  group_by(subject_id, question, chunk_id, position) %>%
  arrange(desc(val)) %>%
  summarise(
    top_func    = first(func),
    top_score   = first(val),
    total_score = sum(val, na.rm = TRUE),
    top_pct     = top_score / total_score * 100,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(is_non_core = top_func %in% non_core_edge)

# chunks to remove: top non-core function holds > 60% of the total
dominated <- chunk_stats %>%
  filter(is_non_core, top_pct > 60)

cat("Edge chunks flagged for removal:",
    nrow(dominated), "out of", nrow(chunk_stats),
    paste0("(", round(nrow(dominated) / nrow(chunk_stats) * 100, 1), "%)"), "\n")
```

```{r chunk-15 }
# apply the filter and recompute normalized time in one pipe so the result is immutable
dominated_keys <- dominated %>% select(subject_id, question, chunk_id)

chunks_scored_prevalence <- chunks_scored_eligible %>%
  anti_join(dominated_keys, by = c("subject_id", "question", "chunk_id"))

chunks_scored_clean <- chunks_scored %>%
  anti_join(dominated_keys, by = c("subject_id", "question", "chunk_id")) %>%
  # drop questions left with only one chunk after edge removal
  group_by(subject_id, question) %>%
  filter(n() > 1) %>%
  # recalculate norm_mid etc. on the remaining chunks
  mutate(
    question_start    = min(start_time, na.rm = TRUE),
    question_end      = max(end_time,   na.rm = TRUE),
    question_duration = question_end - question_start,
    norm_start        = (start_time - question_start) / question_duration,
    norm_end          = (end_time   - question_start) / question_duration,
    norm_mid          = ((start_time + end_time) / 2 - question_start) / question_duration
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>% 
  # we add the log n chunks as a control variable in our models
  group_by(subject_id, question) %>%
  mutate(n_chunks = n_distinct(chunk_id)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(log_n_chunks = log(n_chunks))

cat("Chunks before filtering:", nrow(chunks_scored), "\n")

cat("Removed:", nrow(chunks_scored) - nrow(chunks_scored_clean), "chunks\n")

    chunks_scored %>% distinct(subject_id, question) %>% nrow(), "\n")
cat("Trials after filtering:",
    chunks_scored_clean %>% distinct(subject_id, question) %>% nrow(), "\n")
cat("Removed:",
    chunks_scored %>% distinct(subject_id, question) %>% nrow() -
      chunks_scored_clean %>% distinct(subject_id, question) %>% nrow(),
    "trials\n")
```

```{r chunk-16 }
# Per-outcome (correct vs. biased) exclusion rates at the trial level, so the
# reader can see whether selection into the analysed sample differs by outcome.
# Reported separately for each filtering pass, then for all exclusions together.
exclusion_by_response <- function(from_df, kept_df, pass_label) {
  from_trials <- from_df %>% distinct(subject_id, question, response)
  kept_keys   <- kept_df %>% distinct(subject_id, question)

  total_by_resp <- from_trials %>% count(response, name = "n_trials")
  excluded_by_resp <- from_trials %>%
    anti_join(kept_keys, by = c("subject_id", "question")) %>%
    count(response, name = "n_excluded")

  total_by_resp %>%
    left_join(excluded_by_resp, by = "response") %>%
    mutate(
      n_excluded   = tidyr::replace_na(n_excluded, 0L),
      pct_excluded = round(100 * n_excluded / n_trials, 1),
      pass         = pass_label
    ) %>%
    select(pass, response, n_trials, n_excluded, pct_excluded)
}

exclusion_rates_by_response <- bind_rows(
  # Pass 1: initial >= 2-chunk requirement (chunks_scored_eligible -> chunks_scored)
  exclusion_by_response(chunks_scored_eligible, chunks_scored,
                        "Pass 1: initial >=2 chunks"),
  # Pass 2: edge-domination removal + re-check >=2 chunks (chunks_scored -> chunks_scored_clean)
  exclusion_by_response(chunks_scored, chunks_scored_clean,
                        "Pass 2: edge-domination + >=2 chunks"),
  # All exclusions combined (chunks_scored_eligible -> chunks_scored_clean)
  exclusion_by_response(chunks_scored_eligible, chunks_scored_clean,
                        "All exclusions combined")
)

exclusion_rates_by_response %>%
  kable(col.names = c("Filtering pass", "Response", "Trials",
                      "Excluded", "% excluded"))
```

```{r chunk-17}
exclusion_trials <- chunks_scored_eligible %>%
  distinct(subject_id, question, response) %>%
  left_join(kept_trials,
            by = c("subject_id", "question")) %>%
  mutate(excluded = as.integer(is.na(kept)),
         response = factor(response,
                           levels = c("Correct", "Incorrect")))

exclusion_model <- lme4::glmer(excluded ~ response +
                                (1 | subject_id) +
                                (1 | question),
                              data = exclusion_trials,
                              family = binomial)

exclusion_effect <- broom.mixed::tidy(exclusion_model,
                                      effects = "fixed",
                                      conf.int = TRUE,
                                      conf.method = "profile",
                                      exponentiate = TRUE) %>%
  filter(term == "responseIncorrect")

exclusion_effect
```


### Preparing the modeling dataset

```{r chunk-18 }
# single pipeline for the modeling dataset
chunks_long_clean <- chunks_scored_clean %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols      = all_of(core_cols),
    names_to  = "deliberation_function",
    values_to = "score"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    deliberation_function = recode(deliberation_function, !!!core_labels),
    deliberation_function = factor(deliberation_function),
    response   = factor(response),
    subject_id = factor(subject_id),
    question   = factor(question),
    score_01   = pmax(eps, pmin(1 - eps, score / 100)),
    active     = as.numeric(score > 0)
  ) %>%
  arrange(subject_id, question, chunk_id, deliberation_function) %>%
  mutate(trial_id = factor(interaction(subject_id, question, drop = TRUE)))

# sanity check: score_01 sits strictly inside (0, 1)
summary(chunks_long_clean$score_01)

# distribution of normalized time across chunks, one row per chunk
p_norm_mid_dist <- ggplot(chunks_scored_clean, aes(x = norm_mid)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "steelblue", color = "white", alpha = 0.8) +
  labs(x = "Relative time", y = "Number of chunks") +
  jtools::theme_apa()

p_norm_mid_dist

       plot = p_norm_mid_dist, dpi = 600,
       width = fig_size_wide[["width"]], height = fig_size_wide[["height"]])

```

The score distributions spike at zero for each function, which motivates a hurdle model (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurdle_model): a binomial part (is the function activated at all?) and a beta part (given it is active, what is the intensity?).

```{r chunk-22 }
# helper: boxplot with mean diamond, optionally faceted
plot_box <- function(data, facet_var = NULL) {
  p <- ggplot(data, aes(x = deliberation_function,
                        y = score,
                        fill = deliberation_function)) +
    geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.65, outlier.shape = NA) +
    stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "point", shape = 18, size = 5,

    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 0.65)) +
    labs(x = "Deliberation function", y = "Mean score (0–1 scale)") +
    jtools::theme_apa() +
    theme(legend.position = "none",
          plot.title = element_blank(),
          plot.subtitle = element_blank())

  if (!is.null(facet_var)) p <- p + facet_wrap(as.formula(paste("~", facet_var)))
  p
}
```

## Trajectories

### Overall

We fit two GAMMs: a binomial hurdle for whether each function is active, and a beta intensity model restricted to active chunks. Both include a by-function smooth over normalized time plus random intercepts for subject and question.

```{r chunk-23 }
# zero rates per function (to justify the hurdle model)
chunks_long_clean %>%
  group_by(deliberation_function) %>%
  summarise(
    n        = n(),
    pct_zero = round(mean(score == 0) * 100, 1)
  )

chunks_active <- chunks_long_clean %>%
  filter(active == 1)
```

We check whether we need to add a random intercept per trial.

```{r chunk-24 }
refit_gam_hurdle_fast <- FALSE
refit_gam_hurdle_tid  <- FALSE

# base model
gam_hurdle_fast <- fit_or_load(
  path  = "./Output/Saved_models/gam_hurdle_fast.rds",
  refit = refit_gam_hurdle_fast,
  fit_fun = function() {
    bam(
      active ~ deliberation_function +
        s(norm_mid, by = deliberation_function, k = 20) +
        s(log_n_chunks, k = 5) +
        s(subject_id, deliberation_function, bs = "re") +
        s(question, deliberation_function, bs = "re"),
      family = binomial(link = "logit"),
      data   = chunks_long_clean,
      method = "fREML", discrete = TRUE
    )
  }
)

# same model with trial_id as an additional random intercept
gam_hurdle_tid <- fit_or_load(
  path  = "./Output/Saved_models/gam_hurdle_tid.rds",
  refit = refit_gam_hurdle_tid,
  fit_fun = function() {
    bam(
      active ~ deliberation_function +
        s(norm_mid, by = deliberation_function, k = 20) +
        s(log_n_chunks, k = 5) +
        s(subject_id, deliberation_function, bs = "re") +
        s(question, deliberation_function, bs = "re") +
        s(trial_id,   bs = "re"),
      family = binomial(link = "logit"),
      data   = chunks_long_clean,
      method = "fREML", discrete = TRUE
    )
  }
)

# compareML + AIC; negative deltas favour the trial_id version
compareML(gam_hurdle_fast, gam_hurdle_tid)
```

It seems that it is the case. We refit it using REML.

```{r chunk-25 }
refit_gam_hurdle <- FALSE

# binomial hurdle: is the function active?
gam_hurdle <- fit_or_load(
  path  = "./Output/Saved_models/gam_hurdle.rds",
  refit = refit_gam_hurdle,
  fit_fun = function() {
    gam(
      active ~ deliberation_function +
        s(norm_mid, by = deliberation_function, k = 20) +
        s(log_n_chunks, k = 5) +
        s(subject_id, deliberation_function, bs = "re") +
        s(question, deliberation_function, bs = "re") +
        s(trial_id,   bs = "re"),
      family = binomial(link = "logit"),
      data   = chunks_long_clean,
      method = "REML"
    )
  }
)

tbl_gam(gam_hurdle)

```

```{r chunk-26 }
# we check if number of dim is sufficient
k.check(gam_hurdle)
```


Now we fit the intensity part of the model. We check whether the preferred model benefits from an additional per-trial random intercept.

```{r chunk-27 }
refit_gam_beta_fast <- FALSE
refit_gam_beta_tid  <- FALSE

# fast bam version of the simpler spec for comparison
gam_beta_fast <- fit_or_load(
  path  = "./Output/Saved_models/gam_beta_fast.rds",
  refit = refit_gam_beta_fast,
  fit_fun = function() {
    bam(
      score_01 ~ deliberation_function +
        s(norm_mid, by = deliberation_function, k = 10) +
        s(log_n_chunks, k = 5) +
        s(subject_id, deliberation_function, bs = "re") +
        s(question, deliberation_function, bs = "re"),
      family = betar(link = "logit"),
      data   = chunks_active,
      method = "fREML", discrete = TRUE
    )
  }
)

gam_beta_tid <- fit_or_load(
  path  = "./Output/Saved_models/gam_beta_tid.rds",
  refit = refit_gam_beta_tid,
  fit_fun = function() {
    bam(
      score_01 ~ deliberation_function +
        s(norm_mid, by = deliberation_function, k = 10) +
        s(log_n_chunks, k = 5) +
        s(subject_id, deliberation_function, bs = "re") +
        s(question, deliberation_function, bs = "re") +
        s(trial_id,   bs = "re"),
      family = betar(link = "logit"),
      data   = chunks_active,
      method = "fREML", discrete = TRUE
    )
  }
)

compareML(gam_beta_fast, gam_beta_tid)
```

Adding `trial_id` does not improve the intensity model by much. We fit the simpler specification with REML.

```{r chunk-28 }
refit_gam_beta <- FALSE

# beta intensity given active, no trial_id
gam_beta <- fit_or_load(
  path  = "./Output/Saved_models/gam_beta.rds",
  refit = refit_gam_beta,
  fit_fun = function() {
    gam(
      score_01 ~ deliberation_function +
        s(norm_mid, by = deliberation_function, k = 10) +
        s(log_n_chunks, k = 5) +
        s(subject_id, deliberation_function, bs = "re") +
        s(question, deliberation_function, bs = "re"),
      family = betar(link = "logit"),
      data   = chunks_active,
      method = "REML"
    )
  }
)

tbl_gam(gam_beta)
```

#### Intensity trajectories

```{r chunk-32 }
pred_beta <- map_dfr(
  levels(chunks_long_clean$deliberation_function),
  function(f) {
    get_itsadug_curve(
      gam_beta,
      cond = list(norm_mid = seq(0, 1, length.out = 200),

      keep = "deliberation_function"
    ) %>%
      mutate(deliberation_function = f)
  }
) %>%
  mutate(deliberation_function = factor(deliberation_function,
                                        levels = names(function_colors)[1:4]))

deciles <- seq(0, 1, by = 0.1)

bind_rows(mutate(pred_hurdle, part = "Activation"),
          mutate(pred_beta,   part = "Intensity")) %>%
  group_by(part, deliberation_function) %>%
  group_modify(~ tibble(decile = deciles,
                        fitted = approx(.x$norm_mid, .x$.fitted, xout = deciles)$y)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(fitted = round(fitted, 3)) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = deliberation_function, values_from = fitted) %>%
  arrange(part, decile) %>%
  kable()

  pred_beta,

) +
```

When on, justification is most intense, especially at the end of chunk, as is generation. Control and regulation = not so much happening in terms of intensity.

### By accuracy

First, we check that there is no systematic differences between correct and incorrect trials.

```{r chunk-34}
m_rt <- lmer(log(question_duration_tot) ~ response + (1 | subject_id) + (1 | question),
             data = trial_desc_full)

m_chunks <- glmer(n_chunks ~ response + (1 | subject_id) + (1 | question),
                  family = poisson, data = trial_desc_full)

m_words <- lmer(log(n_words) ~ response + (1 | subject_id) + (1 | question),
                data = trial_desc_full)

summary(m_rt)
summary(m_chunks)
summary(m_words)

# 95% profile-likelihood CIs for the biased-versus-correct contrast
rt_ci <- confint(m_rt,
                 parm = "responseIncorrect",
                 method = "profile")

chunks_ci <- confint(m_chunks,
                     parm = "responseIncorrect",
                     method = "profile")

words_ci <- confint(m_words,
                    parm = "responseIncorrect",
                    method = "profile")

# Ratios: biased / correct
rt_ci
chunks_ci
words_ci

```


We do not observe any systematic differences between trials in terms of RT or number of chunks.

Do activation and intensity trajectories differ between correct and incorrect responses? We add a `deliberation_function * response` interaction and a by-interaction smooth over normalized time. We first check whether this model also benefits from an additional per-trial random intercept.

```{r chunk-35 }
refit_gam_hurdle_acc_fast <- FALSE
refit_gam_hurdle_acc_tid  <- FALSE

# fast bam version of the simple by-accuracy spec, for comparison
gam_hurdle_acc_fast <- fit_or_load(
  path  = "./Output/Saved_models/gam_hurdle_acc_fast.rds",
  refit = refit_gam_hurdle_acc_fast,
  fit_fun = function() {
    bam(
      active ~ deliberation_function * response +
        s(norm_mid, by = interaction(deliberation_function, response), k = 20) +
        s(log_n_chunks, k = 5) +
        s(subject_id, deliberation_function, bs = "re") +
        s(question, deliberation_function, bs = "re"),
      family = binomial(link = "logit"),
      data   = chunks_long_clean,
      method = "fREML", discrete = TRUE
    )
  }
)

gam_hurdle_acc_tid <- fit_or_load(
  path  = "./Output/Saved_models/gam_hurdle_acc_tid.rds",
  refit = refit_gam_hurdle_acc_tid,
  fit_fun = function() {
    bam(
      active ~ deliberation_function * response +
        s(norm_mid, by = interaction(deliberation_function, response), k = 20) +
        s(log_n_chunks, k = 5) +
        s(subject_id, deliberation_function, bs = "re") +
        s(question, deliberation_function, bs = "re") +
        s(trial_id,   bs = "re"),
      family = binomial(link = "logit"),
      data   = chunks_long_clean,
      method = "fREML", discrete = TRUE
    )
  }
)

compareML(gam_hurdle_acc_fast, gam_hurdle_acc_tid)
```

We finally check whether we need to add random slopes by items and participants for accuracy: some questions or participants may show a much larger accuracy contrast than others. Each candidate is compared against `gam_hurdle_acc_tid` (the previous-step winner).

```{r chunk-36 }
compareML(gam_hurdle_acc_tid, gam_hurdle_acc_qslope)

compareML(gam_hurdle_acc_tid, gam_hurdle_acc_bothslope)
compareML(gam_hurdle_acc_qslope, gam_hurdle_acc_bothslope)
# we use model with both random slopes
```

We refit the preferred specification with REML and adopt it as the primary fit.

```{r chunk-37 }
refit_gam_hurdle_acc_final <- FALSE

# primary fit: subject × delib function + trial_id + both random slopes, REML
gam_hurdle_acc <- fit_or_load(
  path  = "./Output/Saved_models/gam_hurdle_acc_bothslope_final.rds",
  refit = refit_gam_hurdle_acc_final,
  fit_fun = function() {
    gam(
      active ~ deliberation_function * response +
        s(norm_mid, by = interaction(deliberation_function, response), k = 20) +
        s(log_n_chunks, k = 5) +
        s(subject_id, deliberation_function, bs = "re") +
        s(question, deliberation_function, bs = "re") +
        s(trial_id,   bs = "re") +
        s(question,   response, bs = "re") +
        s(subject_id, response, bs = "re"),
      family = binomial(link = "logit"),
      data   = chunks_long_clean,
      method = "REML"
    )
  }
)

tbl_gam(gam_hurdle_acc)
```

```{r chunk-38 }
k.check(gam_hurdle_acc)
```

#### Activation differences (Correct − Incorrect)

```{r chunk-46 }
grid_norm_mid <- seq(0, 1, length.out = 200)

diff_hurdle_df <- map_dfr(
  levels(chunks_long_clean$deliberation_function),
  function(f) {
    get_difference(
      gam_hurdle_acc,
      comp = list(response = c("Correct", "Incorrect")),
      cond = list(deliberation_function = f,
                  norm_mid = grid_norm_mid),
      rm.ranef = TRUE,
      sim.ci = TRUE,
      print.summary = FALSE
    ) %>%
      as_tibble() %>%
      mutate(deliberation_function = f)
  }
) %>%
  mutate(deliberation_function = factor(deliberation_function,
                                        levels = names(function_colors)[1:4]))

sig_hurdle_df <- get_sig_segments(diff_hurdle_df)

sig_hurdle_df %>% select(deliberation_function, x, xend) %>% kable(digits = 2)

# black significance band just above the lower y-axis boundary
y_min_traj <- min(pred_hurdle_acc$.lower_ci, na.rm = TRUE)
y_max_traj <- max(pred_hurdle_acc$.upper_ci, na.rm = TRUE)
y_range_traj <- y_max_traj - y_min_traj
y_axis_min_traj <- y_min_traj - 0.08 * y_range_traj

sig_hurdle_traj_df <- sig_hurdle_df %>%
  mutate(y_sig = y_axis_min_traj + 0.03 * y_range_traj)

p_activation_by_response <- p_activation_by_response +
  geom_segment(data = sig_hurdle_traj_df,
               aes(x = x, xend = xend, y = y_sig, yend = y_sig),
               inherit.aes = FALSE,
               color = sig_color,
               linewidth = 1) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(y_axis_min_traj, NA),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05)))

ggsave("./Output/Trajectories/By_accuracy/activation_trajectories_by_accuracy.svg",
       plot = p_activation_by_response, dpi = 600,
       width = fig_size_facets[["width"]], height = fig_size_facets[["height"]])

# put the significance band just above the lower y-axis boundary
y_min_diff <- min(diff_hurdle_df$difference - diff_hurdle_df$CI, na.rm = TRUE)
y_max_diff <- max(diff_hurdle_df$difference + diff_hurdle_df$CI, na.rm = TRUE)
y_range_diff <- y_max_diff - y_min_diff
y_axis_min_diff <- y_min_diff - 0.08 * y_range_diff

sig_hurdle_xax_df <- sig_hurdle_df %>%
  mutate(y_sig = y_axis_min_diff + 0.03 * y_range_diff)

p_activation_diff <- ggplot(diff_hurdle_df, aes(x = norm_mid, y = difference)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = difference - CI, ymax = difference + CI),
              alpha = 0.3, fill = "gray60") +
  geom_line(color = "black", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_segment(data = sig_hurdle_xax_df,
               aes(x = x, xend = xend, y = y_sig, yend = y_sig),
               inherit.aes = FALSE,
               color = "black",
               linewidth = 1.8) +
  facet_wrap(~deliberation_function) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(y_axis_min_diff, NA),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))) +
  labs(x = "Relative time",
       y = "Activation difference\n(Correct − Incorrect)") +
  jtools::theme_apa() +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12),
        panel.spacing = unit(1.0, "lines"),
        plot.title = element_blank(),
        plot.subtitle = element_blank())

p_activation_diff

ggsave("./Output/Trajectories/By_accuracy/activation_difference_correct_minus_incorrect.svg",
       plot = p_activation_diff, dpi = 600,
```

Results are quite clear throughout.

Activation:
- correct: more control at beginning and end, more justification at beginning and end, more regulation throughout
- incorrect: no clear difference

Intensity:
- correct: more control and justification, seems ~quadratic
- incorrect: more generation at the end

## Confidence

We now turn to confidence. We first check whether it correlates with RT, then describe how it evolves across a verbalization and whether it tracks accuracy, and finally we examine the two directional links with deliberation: whether prior confidence predicts the deliberation that follows, and whether prior deliberation predicts the confidence that follows.

### Confidence and response time

We first examine the relation between confidence and response time at the trial level. For each verbalization, we compute the mean confidence across chunks and the total response time as the sum of chunk durations across all chunks.

```{r chunk-52 }
conf_rt_question <- chunks_scored_clean %>%
  mutate(
    subject_id = factor(subject_id),
    question = factor(question)
  ) %>%
  group_by(subject_id, question) %>%
  summarise(mean_confidence = mean(response_confidence, na.rm = TRUE),
            total_rt = first(question_duration_tot),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(log_total_rt = log(total_rt))

p_hist_conf_question <- ggplot(conf_rt_question,
                               aes(x = mean_confidence)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 25, color = "white") +
  labs(x = "Mean confidence across chunks",
       y = "Count") +
  jtools::theme_apa()

p_hist_conf_question

p_hist_rt_question <- ggplot(conf_rt_question,
                             aes(x = log_total_rt)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 25, color = "white") +
  labs(x = "Log RT (s)",
       y = "Count") +
  jtools::theme_apa()

p_hist_rt_question


cor_test <- cor.test(conf_rt_question$mean_confidence,
                     conf_rt_question$total_rt,
                     method = "pearson")

r_val <- round(unname(cor_test$estimate), 2)
p_val <- cor_test$p.value

label_text <- if (p_val < .001) {
  paste0("italic(r) == ", sprintf("%.2f", r_val), "*','~~italic(p) < .001")
} else {
  paste0("italic(r) == ", sprintf("%.2f", r_val), "*','~~italic(p) == ", sprintf("%.3f", p_val))
}

p_conf_rt_question <- ggplot(conf_rt_question,
                             aes(x = mean_confidence, y = log_total_rt)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, color = "red") +
  annotate("text",
           x = -Inf,
           y = Inf,
           label = label_text,
           parse = TRUE,
           hjust = -0.08,
           vjust = 1.5,
           size = 5) +
  labs(x = "Mean confidence",
       y = "Log RT (s)") +
  jtools::theme_apa()

p_conf_rt_question


ggsave("./Output/Confidence/Overall/confidence_response_time_relationship.svg",
       plot = p_conf_rt_question, dpi = 600,
       width = fig_size_single[["width"]], height = fig_size_single[["height"]])

```

We see that our confidence measure averaged at the question level correlates negatively with the total question RT. The negative correlation (r = -0.18), is quite close to the effect size usually observed using confidence ratings (e.g., r = −0.24 in Rahnev et al., 2020, *NHB* in the confidence database).

### Confidence calibration

We next test whether confidence is calibrated with accuracy. For each trial, we average confidence across chunks and ask whether higher confidence corresponds to a higher probability of being correct. Confidence is entered on the logit scale, so perfect calibration would correspond to an intercept of 0 and a slope of 1.

```{r chunk-53, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
# trial-level confidence summary
trial_confidence <- chunks_scored_clean %>%
  arrange(subject_id, question, chunk_id) %>%
  group_by(subject_id, question, response) %>%
  summarise(mean_confidence = mean(response_confidence, na.rm = TRUE),
            correct = as.integer(first(response) == "Correct"),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(subject_id = factor(subject_id),
         question = factor(question),
         confidence_01 = pmin(pmax(mean_confidence / 100, 0.001), 0.999),
         confidence_logit = qlogis(confidence_01))

# observed calibration points, using equal-sized confidence bins
calibration_df <- trial_confidence %>%
  mutate(confidence_bin = ntile(confidence_01, 6)) %>%
  group_by(confidence_bin) %>%
  summarise(mean_confidence = mean(confidence_01, na.rm = TRUE),
            accuracy = mean(correct, na.rm = TRUE),
            n = n(),
            se_accuracy = sqrt(accuracy * (1 - accuracy) / n),
            ci_low = pmax(0, accuracy - 1.96 * se_accuracy),
            ci_high = pmin(1, accuracy + 1.96 * se_accuracy),
            .groups = "drop")

glmer_ctrl <- glmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa",
                           optCtrl = list(maxfun = 2e5))

# a richer random-slope model was checked, but it produced a singular fit
glmer_conf_calibration_slope_check <- glmer(correct ~ confidence_logit +
                                              (1 + confidence_logit || subject_id) +
                                              (1 | question),
                                            data = trial_confidence,
                                            family = binomial(link = "logit"),
                                            control = glmer_ctrl)


# retained calibration model: confidence predicts accuracy, with subject and question intercepts
glmer_conf_calibration_logit <- glmer(correct ~ confidence_logit +
                                        (1 | subject_id) +
                                        (1 | question),
                                      data = trial_confidence,
                                      family = binomial(link = "logit"),
                                      control = glmer_ctrl)

calibration_model_summary <- broom.mixed::tidy(glmer_conf_calibration_logit,
                                               effects = "fixed",
                                               conf.int = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(term = recode(term,
                       `(Intercept)` = "Calibration intercept",
                       confidence_logit = "Calibration slope"),
         odds_ratio = exp(estimate),
         conf.low.or = exp(conf.low),
         conf.high.or = exp(conf.high)) %>%
  transmute(Term = term,
            Estimate = estimate,
            SE = std.error,
            z = statistic,
            p = p.value,
            `OR` = odds_ratio,
            `OR lower 95%` = conf.low.or,
            `OR upper 95%` = conf.high.or)

kable(calibration_model_summary,
      digits = 3,
      caption = "Logit-confidence calibration model predicting trial accuracy.")

# fixed-effect prediction helper with approximate confidence intervals
predict_fixed_glmer <- function(model, newdata) {
  fixed_terms <- delete.response(terms(model, fixed.only = TRUE))
  X <- model.matrix(fixed_terms, newdata)
  beta <- fixef(model)
  V <- as.matrix(vcov(model))

  X <- X[, names(beta), drop = FALSE]

  fit_link <- as.numeric(X %*% beta)
  se_link <- sqrt(diag(X %*% V %*% t(X)))

  newdata %>%
    mutate(fit_link = fit_link,
           se_link = se_link,
           fit = plogis(fit_link),
           lower = plogis(fit_link - 1.96 * se_link),
           upper = plogis(fit_link + 1.96 * se_link))
}

# population-level calibration curve
pred_conf_marginal <- tibble(confidence_01 = seq(min(trial_confidence$confidence_01, na.rm = TRUE),
                                                 max(trial_confidence$confidence_01, na.rm = TRUE),
                                                 length.out = 200)) %>%
  mutate(confidence_logit = qlogis(confidence_01),
         subject_id = trial_confidence$subject_id[1],
         question = trial_confidence$question[1]) %>%
  predict_fixed_glmer(glmer_conf_calibration_logit, .)

# question-specific curves, keeping the question intercepts
question_ranef <- ranef(glmer_conf_calibration_logit)$question

pred_conf_question <- expand_grid(confidence_01 = seq(min(trial_confidence$confidence_01, na.rm = TRUE),
                                                      max(trial_confidence$confidence_01, na.rm = TRUE),
                                                      length.out = 200),
                                  question = levels(trial_confidence$question)) %>%
  mutate(confidence_logit = qlogis(confidence_01),
         subject_id = trial_confidence$subject_id[1],
         question = factor(question, levels = levels(trial_confidence$question))) %>%
  predict_fixed_glmer(glmer_conf_calibration_logit, .) %>%
  mutate(question_intercept = question_ranef[as.character(question), "(Intercept)"],
         fit_question = plogis(fit_link + question_intercept))

p_conf_calibration_glmer_logit <- ggplot() +
  geom_abline(slope = 1,
              intercept = 0,
              linetype = "dashed",
              color = "grey50") +
  geom_line(data = pred_conf_question,
            aes(x = confidence_01,
                y = fit_question,
                group = question),
            color = "grey70",
            linewidth = 0.35,
            alpha = 0.50) +
  geom_ribbon(data = pred_conf_marginal,
              aes(x = confidence_01,
                  ymin = lower,
                  ymax = upper),
              fill = "grey70",
              alpha = 0.35) +
  geom_line(data = pred_conf_marginal,
            aes(x = confidence_01,
                y = fit),
            color = "black",
            linewidth = 1.1) +
  geom_errorbar(data = calibration_df,
                aes(x = mean_confidence,
                    ymin = ci_low,
                    ymax = ci_high),
                width = 0.015,
                color = "black",
                linewidth = 0.45) +
  geom_point(data = calibration_df,
             aes(x = mean_confidence,
                 y = accuracy),
             size = 3,
             color = "black") +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0.2, 0.9),
                  ylim = c(0.1, 0.8)) +
  labs(x = "Mean confidence",
       y = "Accuracy") +
  jtools::theme_apa() +
  theme(plot.title = element_blank(),
        plot.subtitle = element_blank())

p_conf_calibration_glmer_logit

ggsave("./Output/Confidence/Overall/confidence_calibration_question_curves.svg",
       plot = p_conf_calibration_glmer_logit,
       dpi = 600,
       width = fig_size_facets[["width"]],
       height = fig_size_facets[["height"]])
```

Confidence reliably predicts trial accuracy: trials with higher confidence are more likely to be correct. However, the model also shows a negative calibration intercept, indicating a general tendency toward overconfidence. The calibration slope was slightly below the ideal value, but not clearly different from it, suggesting that confidence was informative and globally overconfident, without strong evidence that the confidence scale was severely distorted.


### Confidence over time, by accuracy

We then fit a beta GAMM on confidence as a function of normalized time, with a by-accuracy smooth plus random intercepts for subject and question.

```{r chunk-54 }
# rescale confidence to (eps, 1 - eps) for the beta family
chunks_conf_time <- chunks_scored_clean %>%
  mutate(
    response      = factor(response),
    subject_id    = factor(subject_id),
    question      = factor(question),
    confidence_01 = pmax(eps, pmin(1 - eps, response_confidence / 100)))
```


```{r chunk-55 }
refit_gam_conf_time <- FALSE
n_threads <- max(1, parallel::detectCores() - 1)

gam_conf_time <- fit_or_load(
  path  = "./Output/Saved_models/gam_conf_time.rds",
  refit = refit_gam_conf_time,
  fit_fun = function() {
    gam(
      confidence_01 ~ response +
        s(norm_mid, by = response, k = 10) +
        s(log_n_chunks, k = 5) +
        s(subject_id, bs = "re") +
        s(question,   bs = "re"),
      family   = betar(link = "logit"),
      data     = chunks_conf_time,
      method   = "REML",
      discrete = FALSE,
      nthreads = n_threads
    )
  }
)

tbl_gam(gam_conf_time)
```

Seems like we don't need to add random slopes per accuracy here. This model has one row per chunk (not stacked across the four deliberation functions), so the cross-function dependence that motivates s(trial_id, bs = "re") in the activation models does not apply here. We retain the simpler specification.

### Lagged confidence predicting deliberation

We next ask whether confidence expressed in earlier chunks predicts the activation and intensity of the four core deliberation functions at the current chunk. Chunk confidence is grand-standardized across `chunks_scored_clean` to give `confidence_z`, then decomposed into three orthogonal pieces: `conf_subject_mean` (the participant's overall confidence level — between-subject), `conf_trial_dev` (this trial's mean confidence relative to the participant's mean — between-trial within-subject), and `conf_chunk_dev` (the chunk's confidence relative to its own trial mean — within-trial). Only `conf_chunk_dev` is lagged. The within-chunk slope is the local effect — does a dip in confidence inside a verbalization predict more deliberation at the next chunk — while the trial-deviation and subject-mean slopes capture between-trial and between-subject effects on top of that.

We fit two versions of each model: one with `conf_chunk_dev` at chunk n − 1 only, and one with both n − 1 and n − 2 lags entered together. We also control for the lagged value of the same outcome (prior activation for the hurdle, prior score for the intensity model) so the slope reflects a change in deliberation rather than carry-over. Subject means and trial deviations are computed within each filtered dataset.

```{r chunk-62 }
# threads for fast bam comparisons with discrete = TRUE
n_cores <- max(1, parallel::detectCores() - 1)

# grand-standardized chunk confidence: one z-score across all retained chunks
chunks_conf_lag <- chunks_scored_clean %>%
  arrange(subject_id, question, chunk_id) %>%
  mutate(confidence_z = as.numeric(scale(response_confidence))) %>%
  group_by(subject_id, question) %>%
  mutate(
    # raw lags kept only for the descriptive distribution plot below
    lag_confidence_1 = lag(response_confidence, 1),
    lag_confidence_2 = lag(response_confidence, 2)
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# long format for the four core functions, with same-outcome AR controls
chunks_long_conf <- chunks_conf_lag %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols      = all_of(core_cols),
    names_to  = "deliberation_function",
    values_to = "score"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    deliberation_function = recode(deliberation_function, !!!core_labels),
    deliberation_function = factor(deliberation_function),
    response   = factor(response),
    subject_id = factor(subject_id),
    question   = factor(question),
    score_01   = pmax(eps, pmin(1 - eps, score / 100)),
    active     = as.numeric(score > 0)
  ) %>%
  arrange(subject_id, question, deliberation_function, chunk_id) %>%
  group_by(subject_id, question, deliberation_function) %>%
  mutate(
    lag_active_1   = lag(active, 1),
    lag_active_2   = lag(active, 2),
    lag_score_01_1 = lag(score_01, 1),
    lag_score_01_2 = lag(score_01, 2)
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    lag_active_1 = factor(lag_active_1, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("Inactive", "Active")),
    lag_active_2 = factor(lag_active_2, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("Inactive", "Active")),
    trial_id     = factor(interaction(subject_id, question, drop = TRUE))
  )

# three-level decomposition computed within the filtered dataset.
# subject mean is across the rows of this dataset; trial mean is across chunks
# of one trial; chunk dev is the residual after removing the trial mean.
add_conf_decomposition <- function(df) {
  df %>%
    group_by(subject_id) %>%
    mutate(conf_subject_mean = mean(confidence_z, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    group_by(subject_id, question) %>%
    mutate(
      conf_trial_mean = mean(confidence_z, na.rm = TRUE),
      conf_trial_dev  = conf_trial_mean - conf_subject_mean,
      conf_chunk_dev  = confidence_z - conf_trial_mean
    ) %>%
    arrange(subject_id, question, deliberation_function, chunk_id) %>%
    group_by(subject_id, question, deliberation_function) %>%
    mutate(
      lag_conf_chunk_dev_1 = lag(conf_chunk_dev, 1),
      lag_conf_chunk_dev_2 = lag(conf_chunk_dev, 2)
    ) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    select(-conf_trial_mean)
}

# rows usable for the n−1 and n−1 + n−2 specifications
chunks_long_conf_n1 <- chunks_long_conf %>%
  add_conf_decomposition() %>%
  filter(!is.na(lag_conf_chunk_dev_1),
         !is.na(lag_active_1),
         !is.na(lag_score_01_1))

chunks_long_conf_both <- chunks_long_conf %>%
  add_conf_decomposition() %>%
  filter(!is.na(lag_conf_chunk_dev_1),
         !is.na(lag_conf_chunk_dev_2),

         !is.na(lag_score_01_2))

chunks_active_conf_n1   <- chunks_long_conf_n1   %>% filter(active == 1)
```

We first check whether it benefits from an additional per-trial random intercept.

```{r chunk-65 }
refit_gam_hurdle_conf_n1_fast <- FALSE
refit_gam_hurdle_conf_n1_tid  <- FALSE

  path  = "./Output/Saved_models/gam_hurdle_conf_n1_fast.rds",
  refit = refit_gam_hurdle_conf_n1_fast,
  fit_fun = function() {
    bam(
      active ~ deliberation_function * lag_conf_chunk_dev_1 +
        deliberation_function * conf_trial_dev +
        deliberation_function * conf_subject_mean +
        deliberation_function * lag_active_1 +
        s(norm_mid, by = deliberation_function, k = 10) +
        s(subject_id, deliberation_function, bs = "re") +
        s(question, deliberation_function, bs = "re"),
      family = binomial(link = "logit"),
      data   = chunks_long_conf_n1,
      method = "fREML", discrete = TRUE, nthreads = n_cores
    )
  }
)
```

#### Per-function slopes

Each function gets three slopes per lag specification: a chunk-deviation slope (the local effect — does a within-trial dip in confidence at chunk t − k predict more deliberation at chunk t?), a trial-deviation slope (between-trial within-subject), and a subject-mean slope (between-subject). Slopes are on the logit scale; positive = higher prior confidence predicts more activation / higher intensity.

BH correction is applied within each coefficient family — all four functions tested together for the same component (chunk dev n−1, chunk dev n−2, trial dev, subject mean) within the same model.

```{r chunk-76 }
# tidy emtrends output for one model and one slope variable.
# raw p-values stay so BH can be applied after stacking rows from the same family.
get_slope_table <- function(model, slope_var, model_label, component_label) {
  em <- emtrends(model,
                 specs = ~ deliberation_function,
                 var   = slope_var)

  summary(em, infer = TRUE) %>%
    as_tibble() %>%
    mutate(
      Model     = model_label,
      Component = component_label
    ) %>%
    select(Model,
           Function = deliberation_function,
           Component,
           Slope    = !!paste0(slope_var, ".trend"),
           SE,
           lower.CL,
           upper.CL,
           p.value)
}

# BH within (Model, Component): four functions per family
add_fdr <- function(df) {
  df %>%
    group_by(Model, Component) %>%
    mutate(
      `p (BH)` = p.adjust(p.value, method = "BH"),
      signif = case_when(
        `p (BH)` < 0.001 ~ "***",
        `p (BH)` < 0.01  ~ "**",
        `p (BH)` < 0.05  ~ "*",
        `p (BH)` < 0.1   ~ ".",
        TRUE             ~ ""
      )
    ) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    rename(`p (raw)` = p.value)
}

# all three components from each hurdle model, stacked
slopes_hurdle <- bind_rows(
  get_slope_table(gam_hurdle_conf_n1,   "lag_conf_chunk_dev_1", "n−1 only",  "Chunk dev (n−1)"),
  get_slope_table(gam_hurdle_conf_n1,   "conf_trial_dev",       "n−1 only",  "Trial dev"),
  get_slope_table(gam_hurdle_conf_n1,   "conf_subject_mean",    "n−1 only",  "Subject mean"),
  get_slope_table(gam_hurdle_conf_both, "lag_conf_chunk_dev_1", "n−1 + n−2", "Chunk dev (n−1)"),
  get_slope_table(gam_hurdle_conf_both, "lag_conf_chunk_dev_2", "n−1 + n−2", "Chunk dev (n−2)"),
  get_slope_table(gam_hurdle_conf_both, "conf_trial_dev",       "n−1 + n−2", "Trial dev"),
  get_slope_table(gam_hurdle_conf_both, "conf_subject_mean",    "n−1 + n−2", "Subject mean")
) %>%
  add_fdr()

kable(slopes_hurdle, digits = 3,
      caption = "Per-function slopes of confidence components on activation (logit scale), BH-corrected within (model × component)")
```

#### Activation as a function of lagged confidence

```{r chunk-78 }
# shared plotting helper
plot_lag_curve <- function(pred_df, x_var, x_lab, y_lab, title,
                           y_lim = c(0, 1)) {
  ggplot(pred_df,
         aes(x = .data[[x_var]], y = .fitted,
             color = deliberation_function, fill = deliberation_function)) +
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = .lower_ci, ymax = .upper_ci), alpha = 0.15, color = NA) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
    scale_color_manual(values = function_colors) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = function_colors) +
    coord_cartesian(ylim = y_lim) +
    labs(x = x_lab, y = y_lab, color = NULL, fill = NULL) +
    jtools::theme_apa() +
    theme(plot.title = element_blank(), plot.subtitle = element_blank())
}
```

```{r chunk-79 }
# predicted P(active) sweeping chunk-dev confidence at n−1, one curve per function.
# trial dev and subject mean held at 0; prior activation at the Inactive reference level.
n_grid <- 200

lag_conf_range_n1 <- range(chunks_long_conf_n1$lag_conf_chunk_dev_1, na.rm = TRUE)

pred_lag1_hurdle <- map_dfr(
  levels(chunks_long_conf_n1$deliberation_function),
  function(f) {
    get_itsadug_curve(
      gam_hurdle_conf_n1,
      cond = list(
        lag_conf_chunk_dev_1  = seq(lag_conf_range_n1[1], lag_conf_range_n1[2],
                                    length.out = n_grid),
        deliberation_function = f,
        conf_trial_dev        = 0,
        conf_subject_mean     = 0,
        lag_active_1          = "Inactive",
        norm_mid              = 0.5,
        subject_id            = chunks_long_conf_n1$subject_id[1],
        question              = chunks_long_conf_n1$question[1],
        trial_id              = chunks_long_conf_n1$trial_id[1]
      ),
      keep = "deliberation_function",
      xvar = "lag_conf_chunk_dev_1"
    ) %>%
      mutate(deliberation_function = f)
  }
) %>%
  mutate(deliberation_function = factor(deliberation_function,
                                        levels = names(function_colors)[1:4]))

p_hurdle_lag1 <- plot_lag_curve(
  pred_lag1_hurdle,
  x_var = "lag_conf_chunk_dev_1",
  x_lab = "Chunk-dev confidence at n−1 (z, deviation from trial mean)",
  y_lab = "P(function active)",
  title = "Activation as a function of chunk-dev confidence at n−1"
)

# tweak labels and legend so this plot lines up with the rest of the paper panels
```

### Lagged deliberation predicting confidence

We test the reverse path — does the deliberation engaged in earlier chunks predict confidence at the current chunk? Each deliberation score (control, generation, justification, regulation) is grand-standardized and then decomposed into the same three components used for confidence: a subject mean (`<func>_subject_mean`), a trial deviation (`<func>_trial_dev`), and a chunk deviation (`<func>_chunk_dev`). Only the chunk deviation is lagged. Prior confidence enters as a plain autoregressive control (grand-standardized, lagged), with no decomposition. One row per chunk, so a simple subject + question random-intercept structure (no trial_id, no subject × delib function since the model is univariate).

```{r chunk-83 }
# grand-standardize confidence and the four deliberation scores, then split each
# deliberation score into subject mean, trial dev, and chunk dev. confidence stays
# as a plain z-scored AR control.
chunks_conf_delib <- chunks_scored_clean %>%
  arrange(subject_id, question, chunk_id) %>%
  mutate(across(c(response_confidence, response_control, response_generation,
                  response_justification, response_regulation),
                ~ as.numeric(scale(.x)),
                .names = "{.col}_z")) %>%
  group_by(subject_id) %>%
  mutate(
    control_subject_mean       = mean(response_control_z,       na.rm = TRUE),
    generation_subject_mean    = mean(response_generation_z,    na.rm = TRUE),
    justification_subject_mean = mean(response_justification_z, na.rm = TRUE),
    regulation_subject_mean    = mean(response_regulation_z,    na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  group_by(subject_id, question) %>%
  mutate(
    # trial means
    control_trial_mean       = mean(response_control_z,       na.rm = TRUE),
    generation_trial_mean    = mean(response_generation_z,    na.rm = TRUE),
    justification_trial_mean = mean(response_justification_z, na.rm = TRUE),
    regulation_trial_mean    = mean(response_regulation_z,    na.rm = TRUE),

    # trial dev = trial mean − subject mean
    control_trial_dev       = control_trial_mean       - control_subject_mean,
    generation_trial_dev    = generation_trial_mean    - generation_subject_mean,
    justification_trial_dev = justification_trial_mean - justification_subject_mean,
    regulation_trial_dev    = regulation_trial_mean    - regulation_subject_mean,

    # chunk dev = chunk z − trial mean
    control_chunk_dev       = response_control_z       - control_trial_mean,
    generation_chunk_dev    = response_generation_z    - generation_trial_mean,
    justification_chunk_dev = response_justification_z - justification_trial_mean,
    regulation_chunk_dev    = response_regulation_z    - regulation_trial_mean,

    # lagged chunk devs only
    lag_control_chunk_dev_1       = lag(control_chunk_dev,       1),
    lag_control_chunk_dev_2       = lag(control_chunk_dev,       2),
    lag_generation_chunk_dev_1    = lag(generation_chunk_dev,    1),
    lag_generation_chunk_dev_2    = lag(generation_chunk_dev,    2),
    lag_justification_chunk_dev_1 = lag(justification_chunk_dev, 1),
    lag_justification_chunk_dev_2 = lag(justification_chunk_dev, 2),
    lag_regulation_chunk_dev_1    = lag(regulation_chunk_dev,    1),
    lag_regulation_chunk_dev_2    = lag(regulation_chunk_dev,    2),

    # plain AR lags on z-scored confidence
    lag_confidence_1 = lag(response_confidence_z, 1),
    lag_confidence_2 = lag(response_confidence_z, 2),

    # outcome on the open (0, 1) interval for the beta family
    confidence_01 = pmax(eps, pmin(1 - eps, response_confidence / 100))
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    subject_id = factor(subject_id),
    question   = factor(question),
    trial_id = factor(interaction(subject_id, question, drop = TRUE))
  ) %>%
  select(-control_trial_mean, -generation_trial_mean,
         -justification_trial_mean, -regulation_trial_mean)

# rows usable for the n−1 and n−1 + n−2 specifications
chunks_conf_delib_n1 <- chunks_conf_delib %>%
  filter(!is.na(lag_confidence_1),
         !is.na(lag_control_chunk_dev_1),
         !is.na(lag_generation_chunk_dev_1),
         !is.na(lag_justification_chunk_dev_1),
         !is.na(lag_regulation_chunk_dev_1))

chunks_conf_delib_both <- chunks_conf_delib %>%
  filter(!is.na(lag_confidence_1),
         !is.na(lag_confidence_2),
         !is.na(lag_control_chunk_dev_1),
         !is.na(lag_control_chunk_dev_2),
         !is.na(lag_generation_chunk_dev_1),
         !is.na(lag_generation_chunk_dev_2),
         !is.na(lag_justification_chunk_dev_1),
         !is.na(lag_justification_chunk_dev_2),
         !is.na(lag_regulation_chunk_dev_1),
         !is.na(lag_regulation_chunk_dev_2))

chunks_conf_delib_n1 %>%
  summarise(n = n(), mean_conf = mean(confidence_01), sd_conf = sd(confidence_01))

chunks_conf_delib_both %>%
  summarise(n = n(), mean_conf = mean(confidence_01), sd_conf = sd(confidence_01))
```

We fit a beta GAMM with linear effects of the lagged chunk-dev deliberation scores and their trial-dev and subject-mean components, plus the AR lags on confidence, a smooth of `norm_mid`, and random intercepts for subject and question.

We first check whether the model benefits from a per-trial random intercept.

```{r chunk-84 }
refit_gam_conf_delib_n1_fast <- FALSE
refit_gam_conf_delib_n1_tid  <- FALSE

gam_conf_delib_n1_fast <- fit_or_load(
  path  = "./Output/Saved_models/gam_conf_delib_n1_fast.rds",
  refit = refit_gam_conf_delib_n1_fast,
  fit_fun = function() {
    bam(
      confidence_01 ~ lag_confidence_1 +
        lag_control_chunk_dev_1       + control_trial_dev       + control_subject_mean +
        lag_generation_chunk_dev_1    + generation_trial_dev    + generation_subject_mean +
        lag_justification_chunk_dev_1 + justification_trial_dev + justification_subject_mean +
        lag_regulation_chunk_dev_1    + regulation_trial_dev    + regulation_subject_mean +
        s(norm_mid, k = 10) +
        s(subject_id, bs = "re") +
        s(question,   bs = "re"),
      family = betar(link = "logit"),
      data   = chunks_conf_delib_n1,
      method = "fREML", discrete = TRUE, nthreads = n_cores
    )
  }
)

gam_conf_delib_n1_tid <- fit_or_load(

        lag_generation_chunk_dev_1    + generation_trial_dev    + generation_subject_mean +
        lag_justification_chunk_dev_1 + justification_trial_dev + justification_subject_mean +
        lag_regulation_chunk_dev_1    + regulation_trial_dev    + regulation_subject_mean +
        s(norm_mid, k = 10) +
        s(subject_id, bs = "re") +
        s(question,   bs = "re") +
        s(trial_id,   bs = "re"),
      family = betar(link = "logit"),

      method = "fREML", discrete = TRUE, nthreads = n_cores
    )
```
