#### Per-function effects on confidence

Each deliberation function gets three coefficients per lag specification: chunk dev (the local effect — does a within-trial rise in this function predict a change in confidence at the next chunk?), trial dev, and subject mean. BH correction is applied within each coefficient family — the four functions are corrected together for the same component within the same model.

```{r chunk-89 }
# extract the three-level deliberation coefficients (with emtrends CIs) from one
# model; deliberation_function isn't a factor here, so each term is pulled on its
# own (~ 1), matching the emtrends slope provenance used elsewhere
get_conf_delib_coefs <- function(model, model_label) {
  terms <- broom::tidy(model, parametric = TRUE) %>%
    filter(str_detect(term, "_(chunk_dev_[12]|trial_dev|subject_mean)$")) %>%
    pull(term)

  map_dfr(set_names(terms), function(v) {
    emtrends(model, ~ 1, var = v) %>%
      summary(infer = TRUE) %>%
      as_tibble() %>%
      transmute(term     = v,
                Estimate = .data[[paste0(v, ".trend")]],
                SE       = SE,
                lower.CL, upper.CL,
                p.value)
  }) %>%
    mutate(
      Model = model_label,
      Predictor = case_when(
        str_detect(term, "control")       ~ "Control",
        str_detect(term, "generation")    ~ "Generation",
        str_detect(term, "justification") ~ "Justification",
        str_detect(term, "regulation")    ~ "Regulation"
      ),
      Component = case_when(
        str_detect(term, "_chunk_dev_1$") ~ "Chunk dev (n−1)",
        str_detect(term, "_chunk_dev_2$") ~ "Chunk dev (n−2)",
        str_detect(term, "_trial_dev$")   ~ "Trial dev",
        str_detect(term, "_subject_mean$") ~ "Subject mean"
      )
    ) %>%
    select(Model, Predictor, Component,
           Estimate,
           SE,
           `95% CI low`  = lower.CL,
           `95% CI high` = upper.CL,
           p.value)
}

coef_conf_delib <- bind_rows(
  get_conf_delib_coefs(gam_conf_delib_n1,   "n−1 only"),
  get_conf_delib_coefs(gam_conf_delib_both, "n−1 + n−2")
) %>%
  group_by(Model, Component) %>%
  mutate(
    `p (BH)` = p.adjust(p.value, method = "BH"),
    signif = case_when(
      `p (BH)` < 0.001 ~ "***",
      `p (BH)` < 0.01  ~ "**",
      `p (BH)` < 0.05  ~ "*",
      `p (BH)` < 0.1   ~ ".",
      TRUE             ~ ""
    )
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  rename(`p (raw)` = p.value)

kable(coef_conf_delib, digits = 3,
      caption = "Per-function effects of deliberation components on confidence (logit scale), BH-corrected within (model × component)")
```

```{r chunk-90 }
# n−1 model: one curve per chunk-dev deliberation function at n−1
n1_lag_vars <- c(
  "Control"       = "lag_control_chunk_dev_1",
  "Generation"    = "lag_generation_chunk_dev_1",
  "Justification" = "lag_justification_chunk_dev_1",
  "Regulation"    = "lag_regulation_chunk_dev_1"
)

# every other lagged or component predictor, held at zero when not being swept
n1_zero_vars <- c(
  "lag_confidence_1",
  "lag_control_chunk_dev_1",       "control_trial_dev",       "control_subject_mean",
  "lag_generation_chunk_dev_1",    "generation_trial_dev",    "generation_subject_mean",
  "lag_justification_chunk_dev_1", "justification_trial_dev", "justification_subject_mean",
  "lag_regulation_chunk_dev_1",    "regulation_trial_dev",    "regulation_subject_mean"
)

# shared x-axis so all four curves are on the same scale
shared_range_n1 <- range(unlist(chunks_conf_delib_n1[, unname(n1_lag_vars)]),
                         na.rm = TRUE)

pred_delib_n1 <- imap_dfr(n1_lag_vars, function(var_name, label) {
  cond_list <- list(
    norm_mid   = 0.5,
    subject_id = chunks_conf_delib_n1$subject_id[1],
    question   = chunks_conf_delib_n1$question[1]
  )
  for (v in setdiff(n1_zero_vars, var_name)) cond_list[[v]] <- 0
  cond_list[[var_name]] <- seq(shared_range_n1[1], shared_range_n1[2],
                               length.out = n_grid)

  get_itsadug_curve(
```

### Figure 4 (confidence and lagged effects)

The confidence figure has two panels in one row: A shows confidence trajectories by accuracy, and B shows both lagged directions around a shared set of deliberation functions. Arrow widths are scaled separately within each direction. The association between prior confidence and deliberation intensity is shown in a supplementary figure.

```{r chunk-92 }
loop_y <- setNames(seq(1.35, -1.35, length.out = 4), names(function_colors)[1:4])

bezier_path <- function(x0, y0, x1, y1, curv, n = 60) {
  dx <- x1 - x0
  dy <- y1 - y0
  cx <- (x0 + x1) / 2 + curv * dy / 2
  cy <- (y0 + y1) / 2 - curv * dx / 2
  t <- seq(0, 1, length.out = n)

  tibble(px = (1 - t)^2 * x0 + 2 * (1 - t) * t * cx + t^2 * x1,
         py = (1 - t)^2 * y0 + 2 * (1 - t) * t * cy + t^2 * y1)
}

# panel b of figure 4 is drawn at a fixed print size, so box widths, arrow gaps
# and text share one scale; x and y below are data units per inch of the panel
loop_panel_w <- fig_width_print * 0.60 - 0.15
loop_panel_h <- 2.9 - 0.30
loop_xlim <- c(-3.82, 3.88)
loop_ylim <- c(-1.66, 1.60)
loop_kx <- diff(loop_xlim) / loop_panel_w
loop_ky <- diff(loop_ylim) / loop_panel_h
loop_node_pt <- 7.5

# box half-widths measured from the rendered label, so every arrow can stop
# at the same distance from its box
loop_half_width <- function(label) {
  (systemfonts::string_width(label, family = paper_font, weight = "bold",
                             size = loop_node_pt, res = 72) / 72 / 2 + 0.07) * loop_kx
}
loop_half_height <- (loop_node_pt / 72 / 2 + 0.05) * loop_ky
loop_conf_hw <- loop_half_width("Confidence")

# rounded box outline at exactly that half-width
loop_box_path <- function(x, y, hw, r = 2.5 / 72, n = 8) {
  rx <- r * loop_kx
  ry <- r * loop_ky
  a <- seq(0, pi / 2, length.out = n)
  cx <- c(x + hw - rx, x - hw + rx, x - hw + rx, x + hw - rx)
  cy <- c(y + loop_half_height - ry, y + loop_half_height - ry,
          y - loop_half_height + ry, y - loop_half_height + ry)

  tibble(bx = c(cx[1] + rx * cos(a), cx[2] + rx * cos(a + pi / 2),
                cx[3] + rx * cos(a + pi), cx[4] + rx * cos(a + 3 * pi / 2)),
         by = c(cy[1] + ry * sin(a), cy[2] + ry * sin(a + pi / 2),
                cy[3] + ry * sin(a + pi), cy[4] + ry * sin(a + 3 * pi / 2)))
}

# shared function boxes for the two lagged directions
loop_nodes <- tibble(
  deliberation_function = factor(names(loop_y), levels = names(loop_y)),
  y = unname(loop_y),
  fun_hw = map_dbl(names(loop_y), loop_half_width))

# arrow geometry and label positions for one set of lagged edges
loop_edge_geometry <- function(edges) {
  edges %>%
    left_join(loop_nodes, by = "deliberation_function") %>%
    group_by(direction) %>%
    mutate(sig = signif != "",
           lab = if_else(sig, paste0(sub("^-", "\u2212", sprintf("%+.1f", ame)), signif),
                         NA_character_),
           lwd = scales::rescale(abs(ame), to = c(0.25, 0.95),
                                 from = c(0, max(abs(ame)))),
           # arrows start just under a box border, fanned along its edge, and
           # stop at the same gap from every box
           sx = if_else(direction == "activation", -3 + loop_conf_hw - 0.12, fun_hw - 0.05),
           sy = if_else(direction == "activation", y * 0.05, y),
           ex = if_else(direction == "activation", -fun_hw - 0.07, 3 - loop_conf_hw - 0.07),
           ey = if_else(direction == "activation", y, y * 0.09),
           label_t = if_else(direction == "activation", 0.66, 0.34),
           curv = case_when(
             deliberation_function == "Generation" ~ -0.28,
             deliberation_function == "Justification" ~ -0.05,
             direction == "confidence" & deliberation_function == "Regulation" ~ 0.27,
             deliberation_function == "Regulation" ~ 0.20,
             TRUE ~ 0.12),
           cx = (sx + ex) / 2 + curv * (ey - sy) / 2,
           cy = (sy + ey) / 2 - curv * (ex - sx) / 2,
           lab_x = (1 - label_t)^2 * sx +
             2 * (1 - label_t) * label_t * cx + label_t^2 * ex -
             0.22 * (ey - sy) / sqrt((ex - sx)^2 + (ey - sy)^2) +
             if_else(deliberation_function == "Justification",
                     if_else(direction == "activation", 0.18, -0.30), 0) -
             if_else(direction == "activation" &
                       deliberation_function == "Generation", 0.18, 0),
           lab_y = (1 - label_t)^2 * sy +
             2 * (1 - label_t) * label_t * cy + label_t^2 * ey +
             0.22 * (ex - sx) / sqrt((ex - sx)^2 + (ey - sy)^2) + 0.10 -
             if_else(direction == "activation" &
                       deliberation_function == "Control", 0.14, 0) -
             if_else(direction == "activation" &
                       deliberation_function == "Justification", 0.11, 0) -
             if_else(direction == "activation" &
                       deliberation_function == "Generation", 0.14, 0) -
             if_else(direction == "confidence" &
                       deliberation_function == "Regulation", 0.10, 0)) %>%
    ungroup()
}

loop_edges <- bind_rows(
  mutate(loop_conf_to_activation, direction = "activation"),
  mutate(loop_delib_to_conf, direction = "confidence")) %>%
  loop_edge_geometry()

# draw a set of lagged edges with their function and confidence boxes
plot_loop <- function(edges, confidence_x = c(-3, 3), xlim = loop_xlim) {
  paths <- edges %>%
    mutate(pts = purrr::pmap(list(sx, sy, ex, ey, curv),
                            ~ bezier_path(..1, ..2, ..3, ..4, ..5))) %>%
    tidyr::unnest(pts)

  heads <- paths %>%
    group_by(direction, deliberation_function) %>%
    slice_tail(n = 2) %>%
    ungroup()

  boxes <- bind_rows(
    transmute(loop_nodes, label = as.character(deliberation_function), x = 0, y,
              col = unname(function_colors[as.character(deliberation_function)])),
    tibble(label = "Confidence", x = confidence_x, y = 0, col = "gray30")) %>%
    mutate(id = row_number(),
           hw = map_dbl(label, loop_half_width),
           pts = purrr::pmap(list(x, y, hw), loop_box_path))

  ggplot() +
    geom_path(data = paths,
              aes(px, py, group = interaction(direction, deliberation_function),
                  color = deliberation_function, linewidth = lwd, linetype = sig),
              lineend = "butt", show.legend = FALSE) +
    geom_path(data = heads,
              aes(px, py, group = interaction(direction, deliberation_function),
                  color = deliberation_function, linewidth = lwd),
              linetype = "solid",
              arrow = arrow(length = unit(3.5, "pt"), type = "closed", angle = 25),
              linejoin = "mitre", lineend = "butt", show.legend = FALSE) +
    geom_text(data = edges,
              aes(lab_x, lab_y, label = lab, color = deliberation_function),
              size = 7 / .pt, family = paper_font, fontface = "bold",
              na.rm = TRUE, show.legend = FALSE) +
    geom_polygon(data = tidyr::unnest(boxes, pts),
                 aes(bx, by, group = id, color = I(col)),
                 fill = "white", linewidth = 0.45) +
    geom_text(data = boxes,
              aes(x, y, label = label, color = I(col)),
              size = loop_node_pt / .pt, family = paper_font, fontface = "bold") +
    scale_color_manual(values = function_colors, guide = "none") +
    scale_linewidth_identity() +
    scale_linetype_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "solid", `FALSE` = "11"), guide = "none") +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = xlim, ylim = loop_ylim, expand = FALSE, clip = "off") +
    theme_void() +
    theme(plot.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0))
}
```

**Figure 4.** Confidence dynamics and lagged associations with deliberation. **(A)** Predicted confidence over relative time, separately for correct (green) and biased (red) trials. Confidence increased across correct trials, whereas the slight decline in biased trials was not reliable. Curves are generalized additive mixed model predictions, and shaded bands are simultaneous 95% confidence intervals. The black segment marks the period during which the confidence band for the correct–biased difference excludes zero. **(B)** Bidirectional lagged associations between confidence and deliberation. Left-hand arrows show the average marginal association between a one-SD increase in confidence at chunk *n* − 1 and the probability that each function is active at chunk *n*, in percentage points. Right-hand arrows show the average marginal association between a one-SD increase in each function at chunk *n* − 1 and confidence at chunk *n*, in points on the 0–100 confidence scale. Solid arrows indicate associations that remained reliable after Benjamini–Hochberg correction; dotted arrows indicate associations that did not. \*\* *p* < .01. \*\*\* *p* < .001. Average marginal effects were computed from fixed-effects predictions excluding random effects.

## Predicting response accuracy from deliberation trajectories

We test whether deliberation features predict accuracy for participants and items excluded from model fitting. The five outer participant groups are crossed with leave-one-item-out validation. For each participant-group and item combination, training excludes every trial from that participant group and every response to that item. The test set contains responses from the excluded group to the excluded item. This gives up to 50 outer fits and one held-out prediction per available trial.

Within each outer training set, tuning uses five participant groups crossed with leave-one-item-out validation again. Standardization is learned separately in each training sample. Alpha and lambda are selected using the pooled AUC across all inner held-out predictions. The penalty grid is fixed in advance, and identical outer training samples use the same inner participant splits across feature sets.

The reported AUC is calculated once across all outer held-out predictions, not separately within items or folds. Thus, it includes comparisons across items and separately fitted models. Approximate percentile confidence intervals resample participants within their fixed folds and items independently, using 2,000 crossed-cluster bootstrap draws. The predictions are held fixed in this bootstrap; the intervals do not include variation from rerunning the entire fitting and fold-selection procedure. With only 10 items, uncertainty about generalization across problems remains limited. Final full-sample coefficients are descriptive and are not used to estimate performance.

```{r chunk-96, message = TRUE, warning = TRUE}
library(glmnet)
library(dplyr)

# outer cells are parallelized, but each inner search runs sequentially
n_outer_folds <- 5
n_inner_folds <- 5
n_boot <- 2000
alpha_grid <- seq(0, 1, by = 0.10)
# retain the original penalties and add smaller ones for nearly unregularized fits
lambda_grid <- c(
  10^seq(2, -4, length.out = 100),
  10^seq(-4, -6, length.out = 34)[-1]
)
outer_fold_seed <- 2026
n_workers <- min(4L, max(1L, future::availableCores() - 1L))

ml_cache_dir <- "./Output/Saved_models"
ml_plot_dir <- "./Output/Predicting_accuracy"
dir.create(ml_cache_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(ml_plot_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

previous_ml_plan <- future::plan()
if (n_workers > 1) {
  future::plan(future::multisession, workers = n_workers)
} else {
  future::plan(future::sequential)
}

# linear slope within a trial
safe_slope <- function(y, x) {
  ok <- is.finite(y) & is.finite(x)
  if (sum(ok) < 2 || length(unique(x[ok])) < 2) return(NA_real_)
  coef(lm(y[ok] ~ x[ok]))[2]
}

# normalized position of the largest value within a trial
safe_peak_pos <- function(y, x) {
  ok <- is.finite(y) & is.finite(x)
  if (!any(ok)) return(NA_real_)
  x[ok][which.max(y[ok])]
}

# one row per participant and question
extract_trial_features <- function(df) {
  df %>%
    group_by(subject_id, question, response) %>%
    summarise(
      mean_control           = mean(response_control, na.rm = TRUE) / 100,
      mean_generation        = mean(response_generation, na.rm = TRUE) / 100,
      mean_justification     = mean(response_justification, na.rm = TRUE) / 100,
      mean_regulation        = mean(response_regulation, na.rm = TRUE) / 100,
      slope_control          = safe_slope(response_control / 100, norm_mid),
      slope_generation       = safe_slope(response_generation / 100, norm_mid),
      slope_justification    = safe_slope(response_justification / 100, norm_mid),
      slope_regulation       = safe_slope(response_regulation / 100, norm_mid),
      peak_pos_control       = safe_peak_pos(response_control, norm_mid),
      peak_pos_generation    = safe_peak_pos(response_generation, norm_mid),
      peak_pos_justification = safe_peak_pos(response_justification, norm_mid),
      peak_pos_regulation    = safe_peak_pos(response_regulation, norm_mid),
      mean_confidence        = mean(response_confidence, na.rm = TRUE) / 100,
      confidence_slope       = safe_slope(response_confidence / 100, norm_mid),
      n_chunks               = n(),
      question_duration_tot  = max(end_time, na.rm = TRUE) - min(start_time, na.rm = TRUE),
      n_words                = sum(n_words_chunk, na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      correct = as.integer(response == "Correct"),
      subject_id = factor(subject_id),
      question = factor(question)
    )
}

# one row per participant and question within each temporal quarter
extract_trial_features_by_segment <- function(df, segment_breaks, segment_labels) {
  df %>%
    mutate(
      temporal_segment = cut(
        norm_mid,
        breaks = segment_breaks,
        labels = segment_labels,
        include.lowest = TRUE,
        right = TRUE
      )
    ) %>%
    filter(!is.na(temporal_segment)) %>%
    group_by(temporal_segment, subject_id, question, response) %>%
    summarise(
      mean_control          = mean(response_control, na.rm = TRUE) / 100,
      mean_generation       = mean(response_generation, na.rm = TRUE) / 100,
      mean_justification    = mean(response_justification, na.rm = TRUE) / 100,
      mean_regulation       = mean(response_regulation, na.rm = TRUE) / 100,
      mean_confidence       = mean(response_confidence, na.rm = TRUE) / 100,
      n_chunks              = n(),
      question_duration_tot = max(end_time, na.rm = TRUE) - min(start_time, na.rm = TRUE),
      n_words               = sum(n_words_chunk, na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      correct = as.integer(response == "Correct"),
      subject_id = factor(subject_id),
      question = factor(question),
      temporal_segment = factor(temporal_segment, levels = segment_labels)
    )
}

# feature sets
all_feature_cols <- c(
  paste0("mean_", c("control", "generation", "justification", "regulation")),
  paste0("slope_", c("control", "generation", "justification", "regulation")),
  paste0("peak_pos_", c("control", "generation", "justification", "regulation")),
  "mean_confidence", "confidence_slope",
  "n_chunks", "question_duration_tot", "n_words"
)

external_feature_cols <- c("n_words", "n_chunks", "question_duration_tot")
no_control_feature_cols <- all_feature_cols[!grepl("control", all_feature_cols)]
trajectory_feature_cols <- c(
  paste0("slope_", c("control", "generation", "justification", "regulation")),
  paste0("peak_pos_", c("control", "generation", "justification", "regulation")),
  "confidence_slope"
)
mean_feature_cols <- c(
  "mean_control", "mean_generation", "mean_justification",
  "mean_regulation", "mean_confidence"
)
quarter_feature_cols <- c(
  mean_feature_cols, "n_chunks", "question_duration_tot", "n_words"
)

# labels used in coefficient tables and plots
feature_label_map <- c(
  "(Intercept)" = "Intercept",
  mean_generation = "Generation (mean)",
  mean_justification = "Justification (mean)",
  mean_control = "Control (mean)",
  mean_regulation = "Regulation (mean)",
  mean_confidence = "Confidence (mean)",
  slope_generation = "Generation (slope)",
  slope_justification = "Justification (slope)",
  slope_control = "Control (slope)",
  slope_regulation = "Regulation (slope)",
  confidence_slope = "Confidence (slope)",
  peak_pos_generation = "Generation (peak time)",
  peak_pos_justification = "Justification (peak time)",
  peak_pos_control = "Control (peak time)",
  peak_pos_regulation = "Regulation (peak time)",
  n_chunks = "Number of chunks",
  n_words = "Total words",
  question_duration_tot = "Response time"
)

label_features <- function(x) {
  out <- feature_label_map[as.character(x)]
  out[is.na(out)] <- as.character(x)[is.na(out)]
  out
}

# stop if a model feature is missing or non-finite
check_model_features <- function(data, feature_cols, model_name) {
  missing_cols <- setdiff(feature_cols, names(data))
  if (length(missing_cols)) {
    stop(model_name, " is missing features: ", paste(missing_cols, collapse = ", "))
  }

  bad <- map_lgl(feature_cols, ~ any(!is.finite(data[[.x]])))
  if (any(bad)) {
    stop(model_name, " contains missing or non-finite values in: ",
         paste(feature_cols[bad], collapse = ", "))
  }

  invisible(data)
}

# fit z-scoring parameters on training data
fit_z_scaler <- function(data, feature_cols) {
  map_dfr(feature_cols, function(feature) {
    values <- as.numeric(data[[feature]])
    scale_sd <- sd(values)
    if (!is.finite(scale_sd) || scale_sd == 0) scale_sd <- 1
    tibble(feature = feature, center = mean(values), scale = scale_sd)
  })
}

# apply training z-scoring parameters
apply_z_scaler <- function(data, feature_cols, scaler) {
  x <- as.matrix(data[, feature_cols, drop = FALSE])
  centers <- scaler$center[match(feature_cols, scaler$feature)]
  scales <- scaler$scale[match(feature_cols, scaler$feature)]
  x <- sweep(x, 2, centers, "-")
  sweep(x, 2, scales, "/")
}

# balance folds on correct trials, incorrect trials, and participants
make_balanced_subject_folds <- function(data, nfolds = 5, seed = 1,
                                        n_candidates = 1000) {
  if (n_distinct(data$subject_id) < nfolds) stop("not enough participants for the requested folds")
  set.seed(seed)

  subjects <- data %>%
    group_by(subject_id) %>%
    summarise(
      n_correct = sum(correct),
      n_incorrect = sum(1 - correct),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    arrange(subject_id)

  target_correct <- sum(subjects$n_correct) / nfolds
  target_incorrect <- sum(subjects$n_incorrect) / nfolds

  fold_template <- rep(seq_len(nfolds), length.out = nrow(subjects))
  candidate_folds <- replicate(
    n_candidates,
    sample(fold_template),
    simplify = "matrix"
  )

  candidate_score <- apply(candidate_folds, 2, function(folds) {
    correct_by_fold <- rowsum(subjects$n_correct, folds, reorder = FALSE)[, 1]
    incorrect_by_fold <- rowsum(subjects$n_incorrect, folds, reorder = FALSE)[, 1]
    sum((correct_by_fold - target_correct)^2) / max(target_correct^2, 1) +
      sum((incorrect_by_fold - target_incorrect)^2) / max(target_incorrect^2, 1)
  })

  assigned_fold <- candidate_folds[, which.min(candidate_score)]

  subjects %>%
    transmute(subject_id, fold = assigned_fold)
}

# fixed-direction auc where larger predictions indicate correct responses
auc_binary <- function(correct, prediction) {
  correct <- as.integer(correct)
  n_positive <- sum(correct == 1)
  n_negative <- sum(correct == 0)
  if (n_positive == 0 || n_negative == 0) return(NA_real_)
  prediction_ranks <- rank(prediction, ties.method = "average")
  rank_sum <- sum(prediction_ranks[correct == 1])
  (rank_sum - n_positive * (n_positive + 1) / 2) /
    (n_positive * n_negative)
}

# a test cell contains one participant fold answering one excluded item
# training removes the union of those participants and that item
make_crossed_splits <- function(data, subject_folds) {
  folded <- data %>%
    mutate(subject_id = as.character(subject_id), question = as.character(question)) %>%
    left_join(subject_folds %>% mutate(subject_id = as.character(subject_id)),
              by = "subject_id")
  if (anyNA(folded$fold)) stop("some participants have no fold assignment")
  cells <- folded %>% distinct(fold, question) %>% arrange(fold, question)
  splits <- map(seq_len(nrow(cells)), function(i) {
    held_fold <- cells$fold[i]
    held_item <- cells$question[i]
    train <- which(folded$fold != held_fold & folded$question != held_item)
    test <- which(folded$fold == held_fold & folded$question == held_item)
    if (!length(train) || !length(test)) stop("empty crossed training or test set")
    if (length(unique(folded$correct[train])) != 2L) {
      stop("a crossed training set contains only one response class")
    }
    stopifnot(
      !any(folded$subject_id[test] %in% folded$subject_id[train]),
      !any(folded$question[test] %in% folded$question[train])
    )
    list(train = train, test = test, participant_fold = held_fold,
         held_item = held_item, cell_id = i)
  })
  # every available trial must be tested once, including single-class cells
  stopifnot(identical(sort(unlist(map(splits, "test"))), seq_len(nrow(data))))
  splits
}

# keep the penalty grid fixed before looking at any validation responses
# this also makes penalties comparable across inner training samples
fit_elastic_path <- function(train_data, feature_cols, alpha, lambda_values) {
  scaler <- fit_z_scaler(train_data, feature_cols)
  x <- apply_z_scaler(train_data, feature_cols, scaler)
  if (length(unique(train_data$correct)) != 2L) stop("training requires both classes")
  varying <- apply(x, 2, function(v) diff(range(v)) > 0)
  if (!any(varying)) {
    # a completely constant feature set can only predict training prevalence
    return(list(fit = NULL, scaler = scaler, probability = mean(train_data$correct)))
  }
  previous_control <- glmnet.control()
  on.exit(do.call(glmnet.control, previous_control), add = TRUE)
  glmnet.control(fdev = 0, devmax = 1)
  fit <- glmnet(
    x, train_data$correct, family = "binomial", alpha = alpha,
    lambda = lambda_values, standardize = FALSE, maxit = 100000
  )
  if (fit$jerr != 0 || length(fit$lambda) != length(lambda_values)) {
    stop("an elastic-net path was incomplete; inspect convergence before continuing")
  }
  list(fit = fit, scaler = scaler)
}

predict_elastic_path <- function(object, test_data, feature_cols, lambda_values) {
  if (is.null(object$fit)) {
    return(matrix(object$probability, nrow(test_data), length(lambda_values)))
  }
  x <- apply_z_scaler(test_data, feature_cols, object$scaler)
  predictions <- as.matrix(predict(object$fit, newx = x, s = lambda_values,
                                   type = "response"))
  if (any(!is.finite(predictions))) stop("non-finite predicted probabilities")
  predictions
}

# tune on new participants answering new items inside the outer training set
# pool all inner held-out predictions before computing auc for each candidate
choose_alpha_lambda <- function(train_data, feature_cols,
                                alpha_values = alpha_grid,
                                lambda_values = lambda_grid,
                                nfolds = n_inner_folds, seed = 1, progress = NULL) {
  fold_map <- make_balanced_subject_folds(train_data, nfolds = nfolds, seed = seed)
  splits <- make_crossed_splits(train_data, fold_map)
  results <- map_dfr(alpha_values, function(alpha) {
    held_out <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow(train_data), length(lambda_values))
    for (split in splits) {
      train <- train_data[split$train, , drop = FALSE]
      valid <- train_data[split$test, , drop = FALSE]
      fit <- fit_elastic_path(train, feature_cols, alpha, lambda_values)
      held_out[split$test, ] <- predict_elastic_path(fit, valid, feature_cols, lambda_values)
    }
    if (any(!is.finite(held_out))) stop("incomplete inner held-out predictions")
    if (!is.null(progress)) progress(message = paste("completed alpha", alpha))
    tibble(alpha = alpha, lambda = lambda_values,
           pooled_auc = apply(held_out, 2, function(p) auc_binary(train_data$correct, p)))
  })
  # for exact ties, prefer the larger penalty, then the larger lasso share
  best <- results %>% arrange(desc(pooled_auc), desc(lambda), desc(alpha)) %>% slice(1)
  list(results = results, alpha = best$alpha, lambda = best$lambda,
       inner_auc = best$pooled_auc, inner_folds = fold_map, n_inner_cells = length(splits),
       at_lower_boundary = best$lambda == min(lambda_values))
}

# the final descriptive fit uses the same path as the validation fits
fit_elastic_model <- function(train_data, test_data, feature_cols, alpha, lambda) {
  path <- fit_elastic_path(train_data, feature_cols, alpha, lambda_grid)
  prediction <- as.numeric(predict_elastic_path(path, test_data, feature_cols, lambda))
  if (is.null(path$fit)) {
    values <- c(qlogis(path$probability), rep(0, length(feature_cols)))
    coefficients <- tibble(feature = c("(Intercept)", feature_cols), coefficient = values)
  } else {
    values <- as.matrix(coef(path$fit, s = lambda))
    coefficients <- tibble(feature = rownames(values), coefficient = as.numeric(values))
  }
  coefficients <- coefficients %>% mutate(direction = case_when(
    feature == "(Intercept)" ~ "Intercept",
    coefficient > 0 ~ "Predicts Correct",
    coefficient < 0 ~ "Predicts Incorrect",
    TRUE ~ "Zero"
  ))
  list(fit = path$fit, scaler = path$scaler, prediction = prediction,
       coefficients = coefficients)
}

# only the outer cells run in parallel; inner tuning stays sequential
run_crossed_predictions <- function(data, feature_cols, outer_folds) {
  splits <- make_crossed_splits(data, outer_folds)
  # progress updates arrive as workers finish outer fits, in any order
  results <- progressr::with_progress({
    report_progress <- progressr::progressor(steps = length(splits))
    future_map(splits, function(split) {
      train <- data[split$train, , drop = FALSE]
      test <- data[split$test, , drop = FALSE]
      # identical training samples get identical inner folds across feature sets
      tuning_seed <- outer_fold_seed + 1000L * split$participant_fold +
        match(split$held_item, sort(unique(as.character(data$question))))
      tuning <- choose_alpha_lambda(train, feature_cols, seed = tuning_seed)
      fitted <- fit_elastic_model(train, test, feature_cols, tuning$alpha, tuning$lambda)
      report_progress(message = paste("participant fold", split$participant_fold,
                                      "item", split$held_item))
      list(
        predictions = tibble(
          subject_id = as.character(test$subject_id), question = as.character(test$question),
          correct = test$correct, prediction = fitted$prediction,
          outer_fold = split$participant_fold, outer_cell = split$cell_id,
          held_item = split$held_item, alpha = tuning$alpha, lambda = tuning$lambda
        ),
        audit = tibble(
          outer_fold = split$participant_fold, held_item = split$held_item,
          training_trials = nrow(train), test_trials = nrow(test),
          training_participants = n_distinct(train$subject_id),
          test_participants = n_distinct(test$subject_id),
          training_items = n_distinct(train$question),
          participant_overlap = length(intersect(train$subject_id, test$subject_id)),
          item_overlap = length(intersect(train$question, test$question)),
          inner_cells = tuning$n_inner_cells,
          alpha = tuning$alpha, lambda = tuning$lambda,
          at_lower_boundary = tuning$at_lower_boundary
        ),
        tuning = tuning
      )
    }, .options = furrr_options(seed = TRUE))
  }, handlers = progressr::handler_txtprogressbar(style = 3), enable = TRUE)
  predictions <- bind_rows(map(results, "predictions"))
  stopifnot(nrow(predictions) == nrow(data),
            !anyDuplicated(predictions[c("subject_id", "question")]))
  list(predictions = predictions, audit = bind_rows(map(results, "audit")),
       tuning = map(results, "tuning"))
}


# prepare tied prediction ranks once for the weighted bootstrap calculations
# the pooled auc compares all correct-biased trial pairs, including across items
prepare_auc_data <- function(predictions, prediction_cols = "prediction") {
  if (anyDuplicated(predictions[c("subject_id", "question")])) {
    stop("duplicate participant-item predictions")
  }
  if (anyNA(predictions$correct) || any(!predictions$correct %in% c(0L, 1L)) ||
      any(!is.finite(as.matrix(predictions[, prediction_cols, drop = FALSE])))) {
    stop("invalid outcomes or predictions")
  }
  subject_map <- predictions %>% distinct(subject_id, outer_fold) %>% arrange(subject_id)
  if (anyDuplicated(subject_map$subject_id)) stop("a participant occurs in multiple folds")
  items <- sort(unique(predictions$question))
  ranks <- lapply(prediction_cols, function(column) {
    values <- predictions[[column]]
    match(values, sort(unique(values)))
  })
  list(correct = predictions$correct, ranks = ranks,
       subject = match(predictions$subject_id, subject_map$subject_id),
       item = match(predictions$question, items),
       subject_groups = split(seq_len(nrow(subject_map)), subject_map$outer_fold),
       n_subjects = nrow(subject_map), n_items = length(items))
}

# weighted auc counts ties as one half and always treats correct as positive
weighted_auc <- function(correct, rank_group, weights) {
  by_rank <- rowsum(cbind(positive = weights * correct,
                         negative = weights * (1 - correct)), rank_group, reorder = TRUE)
  positive <- by_rank[, "positive"]
  negative <- by_rank[, "negative"]
  denominator <- sum(positive) * sum(negative)
  if (denominator == 0) return(NA_real_)
  sum(positive * (cumsum(negative) - 0.5 * negative)) / denominator
}

# independently resample participants within their fixed folds and items
# their multiplicities multiply for each observed participant-item trial
# these intervals use fixed held-out predictions, without refitting the models
bootstrap_auc_scores <- function(prepared, n_boot = 2000, seed = 1) {
  set.seed(seed)
  values <- vapply(seq_len(n_boot), function(iteration) {
    subject_counts <- integer(prepared$n_subjects)
    for (group in prepared$subject_groups) {
      drawn <- group[sample.int(length(group), length(group), replace = TRUE)]
      subject_counts <- subject_counts + tabulate(drawn, nbins = prepared$n_subjects)
    }
    item_counts <- tabulate(sample.int(prepared$n_items, prepared$n_items, replace = TRUE),
                            nbins = prepared$n_items)
    weights <- subject_counts[prepared$subject] * item_counts[prepared$item]
    vapply(prepared$ranks, function(ranks) {
      weighted_auc(prepared$correct, ranks, weights)
    }, numeric(1))
  }, numeric(length(prepared$ranks)))
  t(matrix(values, nrow = length(prepared$ranks)))
}

# report usable bootstrap draws and stop if sparse samples make too many undefined
bootstrap_interval <- function(values) {
  valid <- is.finite(values)
  if (mean(valid) < 0.95) stop("fewer than 95% of bootstrap draws had an evaluable auc")
  c(low = unname(quantile(values[valid], 0.025)),
    high = unname(quantile(values[valid], 0.975)))
}

bootstrap_auc <- function(predictions, n_boot = 2000, seed = 1) {
  as.numeric(bootstrap_auc_scores(prepare_auc_data(predictions), n_boot, seed))
}

summarise_prediction_auc <- function(predictions, n_boot = 2000, seed = 1) {
  values <- bootstrap_auc(predictions, n_boot, seed)
  ci <- bootstrap_interval(values)
  list(summary = tibble(
    auc = auc_binary(predictions$correct, predictions$prediction),
    auc_low = ci[["low"]], auc_high = ci[["high"]],
    n_subjects = n_distinct(predictions$subject_id), n_items = n_distinct(predictions$question),
    n_trials = nrow(predictions), n_cells = n_distinct(predictions$outer_cell),
    n_boot_valid = sum(is.finite(values))
  ), bootstrap = values)
}

# paired comparisons use identical test trials, folds, and bootstrap draws
bootstrap_auc_difference <- function(reference, comparison, n_boot = 2000, seed = 1) {
  keys <- c("outer_fold", "subject_id", "question", "correct")
  if (anyDuplicated(reference[keys]) || anyDuplicated(comparison[keys]) ||
      nrow(anti_join(reference, comparison, by = keys)) ||
      nrow(anti_join(comparison, reference, by = keys))) {
    stop("paired model comparisons require identical test trials and folds")
  }
  paired <- reference %>% select(all_of(keys), reference_prediction = prediction) %>%
    inner_join(comparison %>% select(all_of(keys), comparison_prediction = prediction),
               by = keys)
  prepared <- prepare_auc_data(paired, c("reference_prediction", "comparison_prediction"))
  draws <- bootstrap_auc_scores(prepared, n_boot, seed)
  differences <- draws[, 2] - draws[, 1]
  ci <- bootstrap_interval(differences)
  tibble(auc_difference = auc_binary(paired$correct, paired$comparison_prediction) -
           auc_binary(paired$correct, paired$reference_prediction),
         difference_low = ci[["low"]], difference_high = ci[["high"]],
         n_boot_valid = sum(is.finite(differences)))
}

# this full-sample model supplies descriptive coefficients, not test performance
fit_final_descriptive_model <- function(data, feature_cols, progress = NULL) {
  tuning <- choose_alpha_lambda(data, feature_cols, seed = outer_fold_seed + 90000L,
                                progress = progress)
  fitted <- fit_elastic_model(data, data, feature_cols, tuning$alpha, tuning$lambda)
  list(tuning = tuning, fit = fitted)
}

# plot non-zero coefficients from the final model
plot_final_coefficients <- function(coefficients, file_name) {
  plot_data <- coefficients %>%
    filter(feature != "(Intercept)", coefficient != 0) %>%
    mutate(
      feature_lab = label_features(feature),
      feature_lab = fct_reorder(feature_lab, coefficient)
    )

  coefficient_colors <- c(
    "Predicts Correct" = "#369644",
    "Predicts Incorrect" = "firebrick3"
  )

  if (nrow(plot_data) == 0) {
    # a fully shrunk model has only an intercept, so there are no bars to draw
    plot <- ggplot() +
      annotate("text", x = 0, y = 0, label = "no nonzero coefficients retained") +
      theme_void()
  } else {
    plot <- ggplot(
      plot_data,
      aes(x = coefficient, y = feature_lab, fill = direction)
    ) +
      geom_col(alpha = 0.85) +
      geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
      scale_fill_manual(values = coefficient_colors, name = NULL) +
      labs(x = "Elastic-net coefficient (standardized logit scale)", y = NULL) +
      jtools::theme_apa() +
      theme(
        legend.position = "top",
        plot.title = element_blank(),
        plot.subtitle = element_blank()
      )
  }

  ggsave(
    file.path(ml_plot_dir, paste0(file_name, "_coefficients.svg")),
    plot = plot,
    dpi = 600,
    width = fig_size_coeff[["width"]],
    height = fig_size_coeff[["height"]]
  )

  plot
}

# the signature prevents reuse after data, folds, or tuning settings change
crossed_cache_spec <- function(data, feature_cols, outer_folds, seed) {
  list(version = "crossed_validation_v1", data = data, features = feature_cols,
       outer_folds = outer_folds, n_inner_folds = n_inner_folds,
       alpha_grid = alpha_grid, lambda_grid = lambda_grid, n_boot = n_boot,
       split_seed = outer_fold_seed, bootstrap_seed = seed)
}

fit_crossed_model <- function(data, feature_cols, model_name, refit, outer_folds,
                              seed = 1, make_plot = TRUE) {
  check_model_features(data, feature_cols, model_name)
  if (anyDuplicated(data[c("subject_id", "question")])) {
    stop("each model needs one row per participant-item trial")
  }
  if (anyNA(data$correct) || any(!data$correct %in% c(0L, 1L))) {
    stop("outcomes must be coded zero or one")
  }
  signature <- digest::digest(crossed_cache_spec(data, feature_cols, outer_folds, seed))
  path <- file.path(ml_cache_dir, paste0(model_name, "_results.rds"))
  if (!refit && file.exists(path)) {
    saved <- readRDS(path)
    if (identical(saved$signature, signature)) {
      # redraw from the cached coefficients if a plot was removed or restyled
      if (make_plot) saved$p_coef <- plot_final_coefficients(saved$coef_summary, model_name)
      return(saved)
    }
    message("cache settings changed; refitting ", model_name)
  }

  message("fitting ", model_name, " with crossed participant and item holdouts")
  held_out <- run_crossed_predictions(data, feature_cols, outer_folds)
  message("bootstrapping held-out predictions for ", model_name)
  performance <- summarise_prediction_auc(held_out$predictions, n_boot, seed)
  message("tuning the final descriptive model for ", model_name)
  final_model <- progressr::with_progress({
    report_progress <- progressr::progressor(steps = length(alpha_grid))
    fit_final_descriptive_model(data, feature_cols, progress = report_progress)
  }, handlers = progressr::handler_txtprogressbar(style = 3), enable = TRUE)
  coefficients <- final_model$fit$coefficients
  boundary_count <- sum(held_out$audit$at_lower_boundary)
  if (boundary_count > 0 || final_model$tuning$at_lower_boundary) {
    warning(model_name, ": smallest tested lambda (", min(lambda_grid),
            ") selected in ", boundary_count, " of ", nrow(held_out$audit),
            " outer fits; final descriptive fit at boundary: ",
            final_model$tuning$at_lower_boundary,
            ". the fits completed, but a wider grid should be checked before final reporting")
  }
  result <- list(
    signature = signature, model_name = model_name,
    design = "five participant folds crossed with leave-one-item-out",
    feature_cols = feature_cols, predictions = held_out$predictions,
    split_audit = held_out$audit, outer_tuning = held_out$tuning,
    auc_summary = performance$summary %>% mutate(
      design = "five participant folds crossed with leave-one-item-out", .before = 1,
      alpha = final_model$tuning$alpha, lambda = final_model$tuning$lambda
    ),
    bootstrap_auc = performance$bootstrap, final_model = final_model,
    coef_summary = coefficients,
    p_coef = if (make_plot) plot_final_coefficients(coefficients, model_name) else NULL
  )
  saveRDS(result, path)
  result
}

trial_features <- extract_trial_features(chunks_scored_clean)
```

### Correlations Among Prediction Features

```{r chunk-97, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 9}
# one row per trial, using the same 17 predictors as the full classifier
x <- as.matrix(trial_features[, all_feature_cols])
stopifnot(all(is.finite(x)), all(apply(x, 2, sd) > 0))
pairs <- which(lower.tri(cor(x)), arr.ind = TRUE)

# pearson correlations, with correction across all 136 unique pairs
correlations <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(pairs)), function(k) {
  i <- pairs[k, 1]
  j <- pairs[k, 2]
  test <- cor.test(x[, i], x[, j], method = "pearson")
  tibble(feature_y = colnames(x)[i], feature_x = colnames(x)[j],
         r = unname(test$estimate), p = test$p.value)
})) %>% mutate(p_adjusted = p.adjust(p, method = "BH"), supported = p_adjusted < .05)

# show one triangle; leave nonsignificant cells white
feature_labels <- unname(feature_label_map[all_feature_cols])
cor_plot_data <- correlations %>% mutate(
  feature_x = factor(feature_x, levels = all_feature_cols, labels = feature_labels),
  feature_y = factor(feature_y, levels = rev(all_feature_cols), labels = rev(feature_labels)),
  fill_r = if_else(supported, r, NA_real_),
  label = if_else(supported, sub("^(-?)0", "\\1", sprintf("%.2f", r)), "")
)
p_feature_correlations <- ggplot(cor_plot_data, aes(feature_x, feature_y)) +
  geom_tile(aes(fill = fill_r), color = "grey90", linewidth = 0.25) +
  geom_text(aes(label = label, color = supported & abs(r) >= .60), size = 2.6) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("FALSE" = "black", "TRUE" = "white"), guide = "none") +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#2166AC", mid = "white", high = "#B2182B",
                       limits = c(-1, 1), na.value = "white", name = "Pearson r") +
  scale_x_discrete(drop = FALSE, expand = expansion(add = .5)) +
  scale_y_discrete(drop = FALSE, expand = expansion(add = .5)) +
  coord_fixed() + labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) + jtools::theme_apa() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 10),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10), axis.ticks = element_blank(),
        axis.line = element_blank(), panel.border = element_blank(),
        panel.grid = element_blank(), legend.position = "right")
p_feature_correlations

dir.create("./Output/Figures_paper", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
ggsave("./Output/Figures_paper/Supplementary_figure_prediction_feature_correlations.svg",
       p_feature_correlations, width = 10, height = 9, bg = "white")
write.csv(correlations, file.path(ml_plot_dir, "prediction_feature_correlations.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)
```

**Supplementary Figure.** Correlations among the 17 prediction features across 565 trials. The lower triangle shows Pearson correlations, with the diagonal omitted. Colored cells and numerical labels indicate correlations with Benjamini–Hochberg-adjusted *p* < .05 across 136 comparisons; nonsignificant cells are white. These exploratory tests treat trials as independent and do not account for repeated observations from the same participants or items.

### Whole-trial prediction

The full model uses all 17 features. Each held-out prediction excludes both its participant group and its item from fitting, scaling, and tuning.

```{r chunk-98, message = TRUE, warning = TRUE}
elastic_full <- fit_crossed_model(
  trial_features, all_feature_cols, model_name = "elastic_full_crossed",
  refit = refit_ml_full, outer_folds = outer_subject_folds, seed = 100
)
kable(elastic_full$auc_summary, digits = 3, caption = "pooled held-out auc for the full model")
kable(elastic_full$split_audit, digits = 3, caption = "outer split and tuning checks")
elastic_full$p_coef
```

### Temporal prediction by quarter

Each quarter uses its own mean scores and length features, with no cumulative information from earlier quarters. All quarters share the outer participant assignments and use the same crossed validation procedure. A trial contributes only when a chunk midpoint falls in that quarter.

```{r chunk-99, message = TRUE, warning = TRUE}
segment_breaks <- seq(0, 1, by = 0.25)
segment_labels <- c("0-25%", "25-50%", "50-75%", "75-100%")

trial_features_quarters <- extract_trial_features_by_segment(
  chunks_scored_clean,
  segment_breaks = segment_breaks,
  segment_labels = segment_labels
)

quarter_participant_counts <- trial_features_quarters %>%
  count(temporal_segment, subject_id, name = "participant_trials")

trials_in_all_quarters <- trial_features_quarters %>%
  distinct(temporal_segment, subject_id, question) %>%
  count(subject_id, question) %>%
  filter(n == length(segment_labels)) %>%
  nrow()

quarter_trial_summary <- trial_features_quarters %>%
  group_by(temporal_segment) %>%
  summarise(
    participants = n_distinct(subject_id),
    trials = n(),
    correct_trials = sum(correct),
    incorrect_trials = sum(correct == 0),
    accuracy = mean(correct),
    median_chunks_per_trial = median(n_chunks),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  rename(
    correct = correct_trials,
    incorrect = incorrect_trials
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    quarter_participant_counts %>%
      group_by(temporal_segment) %>%
      summarise(
        median_trials_per_participant = median(participant_trials),
        .groups = "drop"
      ),
    by = "temporal_segment"
  ) %>%
  mutate(trials_in_all_quarters = trials_in_all_quarters)

kable(
  quarter_trial_summary,
  digits = 3,
  caption = "Trials represented in each temporal quarter"
)

# cache quarters individually so completed models remain available after an interruption
quarter_models <- setNames(map(segment_labels, function(segment) {
  segment_data <- trial_features_quarters %>%
    filter(temporal_segment == segment) %>% droplevels()
  fit_crossed_model(
    segment_data, quarter_feature_cols,
    model_name = paste0("elastic_quarter_", gsub("%|-", "", segment), "_crossed"),
    refit = refit_ml_temporal_quarters, outer_folds = outer_subject_folds,
    seed = 200 + match(segment, segment_labels)
  )
}), segment_labels)
```

#### Temporal prediction in trials represented in every quarter

This robustness check holds the evaluation sample constant across time. It restricts the existing participant-and-item-held-out predictions to participant-item trials containing at least one chunk midpoint in every temporal quarter. The models are not refitted.

```{r chunk-100 }
  )$summary %>% mutate(temporal_segment = factor(segment, levels = segment_labels),
                       .before = 1)
})
```

### Reduced feature sets

The length-only model tests prediction from number of chunks, response time, and word count. The no-control model removes control mean, slope, and peak position. The trajectory-only model uses four function slopes, four peak positions, and confidence slope. All use the same crossed outer holdouts as the full model. Paired comparisons use identical trials and crossed-cluster bootstrap draws.

```{r chunk-101, message = TRUE, warning = TRUE}
elastic_external <- fit_crossed_model(
  trial_features, external_feature_cols, model_name = "elastic_external_crossed",
  refit = refit_ml_external, outer_folds = outer_subject_folds, seed = 300
)
elastic_no_control <- fit_crossed_model(
  trial_features, no_control_feature_cols, model_name = "elastic_no_control_crossed",
  refit = refit_ml_no_control, outer_folds = outer_subject_folds, seed = 400
)
elastic_trajectory_only <- fit_crossed_model(
  trial_features, trajectory_feature_cols, model_name = "elastic_trajectory_only_crossed",
  refit = refit_ml_trajectory_only, outer_folds = outer_subject_folds, seed = 450
)

robustness_auc <- bind_rows(
  "full model" = elastic_full$auc_summary,
  "without control" = elastic_no_control$auc_summary,
  "trajectory only" = elastic_trajectory_only$auc_summary,
  "length only" = elastic_external$auc_summary,
  .id = "model"
)
kable(robustness_auc, digits = 3, caption = "pooled held-out auc across feature sets")

reduced_models <- list(
  "without control" = elastic_no_control,
  "trajectory only" = elastic_trajectory_only,
  "length only" = elastic_external
)
model_auc_differences <- imap_dfr(reduced_models, function(model, name) {
  bootstrap_auc_difference(model$predictions, elastic_full$predictions,
                           n_boot = n_boot, seed = 475) %>%
    mutate(comparison = paste("full model minus", name), .before = 1)
})
kable(model_auc_differences, digits = 3,
      caption = "paired auc differences between full and reduced models")
elastic_trajectory_only$p_coef
```

### Figure 3 (by-accuracy trajectories)

The three rows show participant mean function scores by accuracy, followed by activation and intensity trajectories. The score distributions include single-chunk trials, as in Figure 2B. All rows share the same function order and accuracy colors. The whole-trial coefficients are reported in Table 3, and AUC by temporal quarter is shown separately in the supplementary figure below.

```{r chunk-103, fig.width = 6.3, fig.height = 6.8}
# panel a prevalence by accuracy
fig3_scores_subject <- chunks_long_question %>%
  group_by(subject_id, deliberation_function, response) %>%
  summarise(score = mean(score) * 100, .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(deliberation_function = factor(deliberation_function,
                                         levels = names(function_colors)[1:4]))

fig3_prevalence <- ggplot(fig3_scores_subject,
                          aes(x = response, y = score, fill = response, color = response)) +
  geom_violin(width = 0.85, trim = FALSE, alpha = 0.25,
              scale = "width", linewidth = 0.35) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.18, outlier.shape = NA, fill = "white", linewidth = 0.35) +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "point", shape = 23, size = 1.5,
               fill = "#222222", color = "white", stroke = 0.3) +
  facet_wrap(~ deliberation_function, nrow = 1) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = response_colors, guide = "none") +
  scale_color_manual(values = response_colors, guide = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 100, 20),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.02))) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, max(70, fig3_scores_subject$score, na.rm = TRUE))) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Mean function score") +
  theme_paper_print() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(), axis.ticks.x = element_blank())

# panels b and c share one layout: curves by accuracy, black significance band
fig3_trajectory <- function(pred, sig, ylab, scale = 1, y_min) {
  ggplot(pred, aes(x = norm_mid, y = .fitted * scale, color = response, fill = response)) +
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = .lower_ci * scale, ymax = .upper_ci * scale),
                alpha = 0.16, color = NA) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.6) +
    geom_segment(data = sig,
                 aes(x = x, xend = xend, y = y_sig, yend = y_sig),
                 inherit.aes = FALSE,
                 color = sig_color,
                 linewidth = 0.9) +
    facet_wrap(~ deliberation_function, nrow = 1) +
    scale_color_manual(values = response_colors,
                       labels = c(Correct = "Correct", Incorrect = "Biased")) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = response_colors,
                      labels = c(Correct = "Correct", Incorrect = "Biased")) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(0, 0.5, 1), labels = c("0", "0.5", "1"),
                       expand = expansion(mult = 0.03)) +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(y_min, NA), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.04))) +
    labs(x = "Relative time", y = ylab) +
    paper_print_legend("Response") +
    theme_paper_print()
}

# panel c intensity by accuracy

                  plot_layout(heights = c(0.85, 1, 1)) +
```

**Figure 3.** Deliberation dynamics distinguish correct from biased reasoning. **(A)** Participant mean function scores for correct (green) and biased (red) trials. Scores were averaged across chunks within each trial and then across trials within each participant and response category. Violins show the distributions of participant means; boxes show the interquartile range, horizontal lines mark medians, and black diamonds mark means. **(B)** Predicted probability that each function is active. Correct trials show a greater likelihood of justification, control and regulation being active, but no detectable difference in generation. **(C)** Predicted score for each function when it is active. Correct trials show higher justification and control scores, and lower generation scores. Curves in B and C are generalized additive mixed model predictions from the hurdle model, and shaded bands are simultaneous 95% confidence intervals. Black horizontal segments mark the periods where the confidence band of the correct–biased difference excludes zero. Relative time is each chunk's midpoint expressed relative to the span of retained chunks (0 = first, 1 = last).

```{r chunk-104, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5}
                       expand = expansion(mult = 0)) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0.40, 0.90), clip = "off") +
    labs(x = "Trial segment", y = "Held-out AUC") +
    jtools::theme_apa() +
    theme(plot.title = element_blank(), plot.subtitle = element_blank(),
      axis.title.x = element_text(margin = margin(t = 8))))

fig_auc_quarters

ggsave("./Output/Figures_paper/Supplementary_figure_temporal_quarters_crossed.svg",
       plot = fig_auc_quarters,
       dpi = 600,
       width = fig_size_single[["width"]],
       height = fig_size_single[["height"]])
```

**Supplementary Figure.** Prediction accuracy across temporal quarters. Each model is evaluated on participants and items excluded from its fitting, scaling, and tuning. Points show pooled AUCs across all outer held-out predictions; error bars show approximate 95% percentile intervals from 2,000 bootstrap draws resampling participants and items independently. The dashed line marks chance discrimination, and the dotted line marks the full-trial AUC. The figure is descriptive; differences between quarters require paired comparisons on common trials. AUC = area under the receiver operating characteristic curve.

## Robustness Analyses

### Edge-chunk and activation threshold sensitivity

The main analyses make two design choices that warrant a sensitivity check: which chunks to remove at the edges of each verbalization, and what counts as an "active" expression of a deliberation function. We re-fit every GAMM under four scenarios. The first three vary the edge-chunk filter — the original 60/60 threshold (drop edge chunks dominated by Repetition or Answer Selection at >60%), no filtering at all, and an aggressive 0/0 threshold that removes every edge chunk dominated by either function. The fourth keeps the original edge filter but raises the activation threshold from > 0 to > 5, so chunks with very weak signal (≤ 5 on the 0–100 scale) count as inactive. For the trajectory and by-accuracy models we plot the fitted curves (and Correct − Incorrect difference curves) faceted by scenario; for the lagged confidence ↔ deliberation models we report compact comparison tables of within-trial slopes / coefficients with BH-corrected significance, scenario by scenario.

```{r chunk-105 }
# four robustness scenarios
# the first three vary edge filtering at 20% edges; the fourth keeps the original
# edge filter but redefines a function as "active" only when score > 5
robustness_scenarios <- tibble::tribble(
  ~label,                   ~edge_cutoff, ~pct_repetition, ~pct_answer_sel, ~active_threshold,
  "original (60/60, > 0)",  0.20,         60,              60,              0,
  "no filtering (> 0)",     NA_real_,     NA_real_,        NA_real_,        0,
  "aggressive (0/0, > 0)",  0.20,         0,               0,               0,
  "activation > 5",         0.20,         60,              60,              5
)

scenario_levels <- robustness_scenarios$label

# display names for the scenario panels; the labels above stay as cache keys
scenario_labels <- setNames(c("Original rule", "No edge filtering",
                              "Stricter edge filtering", "Activation threshold > 5"),
                            scenario_levels)
```

```{r chunk-106 }
# build the cleaned chunk-level dataset for one edge-filter combination
# the activation threshold is applied later, in prep_data, so the same cleaned
# dataset can be reused with different activation thresholds
build_clean_at <- function(edge_cutoff, pct_repetition, pct_answer_sel) {
  if (is.na(edge_cutoff)) return(chunks_scored)

  to_drop <- chunks_scored %>%
    filter(norm_mid < edge_cutoff | norm_mid > 1 - edge_cutoff) %>%
    pivot_longer(all_of(edge_cols), names_to = "func", values_to = "val") %>%
    mutate(func = recode(func, !!!edge_labels)) %>%
    group_by(subject_id, question, chunk_id) %>%
    summarise(top_func = func[which.max(val)],
              top_pct  = max(val) / sum(val, na.rm = TRUE) * 100,
              .groups  = "drop") %>%
    filter((top_func == "Repetition"       & top_pct > pct_repetition) |
           (top_func == "Answer Selection" & top_pct > pct_answer_sel)) %>%
    select(subject_id, question, chunk_id)

  # drop flagged chunks, recompute normalized time, toss questions with one chunk
  chunks_scored %>%
    anti_join(to_drop, by = c("subject_id", "question", "chunk_id")) %>%
    group_by(subject_id, question) %>%
    filter(n() > 1) %>%
    mutate(question_start    = min(start_time, na.rm = TRUE),
           question_duration = max(end_time, na.rm = TRUE) - question_start,
           norm_mid          = ((start_time + end_time) / 2 - question_start) /
                               question_duration) %>%
    ungroup()
}
```

The data prep mirrors the main analyses: confidence and the four deliberation scores are grand-standardized once across the cleaned dataset, then each is decomposed into a subject mean (between-subject baseline), a trial deviation (between-trial within subject), and a chunk deviation (within-trial). Only the chunk deviation is lagged. The activation threshold is applied to the long-format dataset so the same cleaned dataset can serve different cutoffs.

```{r chunk-107 }
# every long-format dataset needed by the robustness models, with the
# three-level decomposition for confidence and for each deliberation predictor
prep_data <- function(clean_df, active_threshold = 0) {

  # recompute n_chunks on the post-filter data so log_n_chunks reflects the scenario
  clean_df <- clean_df %>%
    group_by(subject_id, question) %>%
    mutate(n_chunks = n_distinct(chunk_id)) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    mutate(log_n_chunks = log(n_chunks))

  # grand-standardize confidence and each deliberation score once
  clean_df <- clean_df %>%
    arrange(subject_id, question, chunk_id) %>%
    mutate(
      confidence_z = as.numeric(scale(response_confidence)),
      across(c(response_control, response_generation,
               response_justification, response_regulation),
             ~ as.numeric(scale(.x)),
             .names = "{.col}_z")
    )

  # long format with same-outcome AR controls
  to_long <- function(df) {
    df %>%
      pivot_longer(all_of(core_cols),
                   names_to = "deliberation_function", values_to = "score") %>%
      mutate(deliberation_function = factor(recode(deliberation_function, !!!core_labels)),
             response   = factor(response),
             subject_id = factor(subject_id),
             question   = factor(question),
             trial_id   = factor(as.character(trial_id)),
             score_01   = pmax(eps, pmin(1 - eps, score / 100)),
             active     = as.numeric(score > active_threshold))
  }

  long <- to_long(clean_df) %>%
    arrange(subject_id, question, deliberation_function, chunk_id) %>%
    group_by(subject_id, question, deliberation_function) %>%
    mutate(lag_active_1   = lag(active, 1),
           lag_active_2   = lag(active, 2),
           lag_score_01_1 = lag(score_01, 1),
           lag_score_01_2 = lag(score_01, 2)) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    mutate(lag_active_1 = factor(lag_active_1, c(0, 1), c("Inactive", "Active")),
           lag_active_2 = factor(lag_active_2, c(0, 1), c("Inactive", "Active")))

  # three-level decomposition for confidence on the long table
  long_conf <- long %>%
    group_by(subject_id) %>%
    mutate(conf_subject_mean = mean(confidence_z, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    group_by(subject_id, question) %>%
    mutate(conf_trial_mean = mean(confidence_z, na.rm = TRUE),
           conf_trial_dev  = conf_trial_mean - conf_subject_mean,
           conf_chunk_dev  = confidence_z - conf_trial_mean) %>%
    arrange(subject_id, question, deliberation_function, chunk_id) %>%
    group_by(subject_id, question, deliberation_function) %>%
    mutate(lag_conf_chunk_dev_1 = lag(conf_chunk_dev, 1),
           lag_conf_chunk_dev_2 = lag(conf_chunk_dev, 2)) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    select(-conf_trial_mean)

  conf_n1   <- long_conf %>% drop_na(lag_conf_chunk_dev_1, conf_trial_dev,
                                     conf_subject_mean,
                                     lag_active_1, lag_score_01_1)
  conf_both <- long_conf %>% drop_na(lag_conf_chunk_dev_1, lag_conf_chunk_dev_2,
                                     conf_trial_dev, conf_subject_mean,
                                     lag_active_1, lag_active_2,
                                     lag_score_01_1, lag_score_01_2)

  # three-level decomposition for each deliberation score (chunk-level, no pivot);
  # confidence stays as a plain z-scored AR control
  delib <- clean_df %>%
    group_by(subject_id) %>%
    mutate(
      control_subject_mean       = mean(response_control_z,       na.rm = TRUE),
      generation_subject_mean    = mean(response_generation_z,    na.rm = TRUE),
      justification_subject_mean = mean(response_justification_z, na.rm = TRUE),
      regulation_subject_mean    = mean(response_regulation_z,    na.rm = TRUE)
    ) %>%
    group_by(subject_id, question) %>%
    mutate(
      control_trial_mean       = mean(response_control_z,       na.rm = TRUE),
      generation_trial_mean    = mean(response_generation_z,    na.rm = TRUE),
      justification_trial_mean = mean(response_justification_z, na.rm = TRUE),
      regulation_trial_mean    = mean(response_regulation_z,    na.rm = TRUE),

      control_trial_dev       = control_trial_mean       - control_subject_mean,
      generation_trial_dev    = generation_trial_mean    - generation_subject_mean,
      justification_trial_dev = justification_trial_mean - justification_subject_mean,
      regulation_trial_dev    = regulation_trial_mean    - regulation_subject_mean,

      control_chunk_dev       = response_control_z       - control_trial_mean,
      generation_chunk_dev    = response_generation_z    - generation_trial_mean,
      justification_chunk_dev = response_justification_z - justification_trial_mean,
      regulation_chunk_dev    = response_regulation_z    - regulation_trial_mean,

      lag_control_chunk_dev_1       = lag(control_chunk_dev,       1),
      lag_control_chunk_dev_2       = lag(control_chunk_dev,       2),
      lag_generation_chunk_dev_1    = lag(generation_chunk_dev,    1),
      lag_generation_chunk_dev_2    = lag(generation_chunk_dev,    2),
      lag_justification_chunk_dev_1 = lag(justification_chunk_dev, 1),
      lag_justification_chunk_dev_2 = lag(justification_chunk_dev, 2),
      lag_regulation_chunk_dev_1    = lag(regulation_chunk_dev,    1),
      lag_regulation_chunk_dev_2    = lag(regulation_chunk_dev,    2),

      lag_confidence_1 = lag(confidence_z, 1),
      lag_confidence_2 = lag(confidence_z, 2),

      confidence_01    = pmax(eps, pmin(1 - eps, response_confidence / 100))
    ) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    mutate(response   = factor(response),
           subject_id = factor(subject_id),
           question   = factor(question),
           trial_id   = factor(as.character(trial_id))) %>%
    select(-ends_with("_trial_mean"))

  delib_n1   <- delib %>% drop_na(lag_confidence_1,
                                  lag_control_chunk_dev_1,
                                  lag_generation_chunk_dev_1,
                                  lag_justification_chunk_dev_1,
                                  lag_regulation_chunk_dev_1)
  delib_both <- delib %>% drop_na(lag_confidence_1, lag_confidence_2,
                                  lag_control_chunk_dev_1, lag_control_chunk_dev_2,
                                  lag_generation_chunk_dev_1, lag_generation_chunk_dev_2,
                                  lag_justification_chunk_dev_1, lag_justification_chunk_dev_2,
                                  lag_regulation_chunk_dev_1, lag_regulation_chunk_dev_2)

  list(long       = long,
       active     = long %>% filter(active == 1),
       conf_n1    = conf_n1,
       conf_both  = conf_both,
       active_conf_n1   = conf_n1   %>% filter(active == 1),
       active_conf_both = conf_both %>% filter(active == 1),
       delib_n1   = delib_n1,
       delib_both = delib_both)
}
```

Each scenario fits the same set of GAMMs as the main analyses, with random structures and controls matching the final retained models. All fits use `bam` with `fREML` and `discrete = TRUE` to keep the four-scenario sweep tractable.

```{r chunk-108 }
# fit every robustness model for one cleaned dataset and one activation threshold
fit_scenario <- function(clean_df, active_threshold = 0) {
  d <- prep_data(clean_df, active_threshold = active_threshold)

  bam_fast <- function(formula, family, data) {
    bam(formula, family = family, data = data,
        method = "fREML", discrete = TRUE)
  }

  list(
    data = d,

    # overall hurdle: subject and question random slopes by function, plus trial_id
    hurdle = bam_fast(
      active ~ deliberation_function +
        s(norm_mid, by = deliberation_function, k = 20) +
        s(log_n_chunks, k = 5) +
        s(subject_id, deliberation_function, bs = "re") +
        s(question,   deliberation_function, bs = "re") +
        s(trial_id,   bs = "re"),
      binomial(link = "logit"), d$long),

    # overall intensity: same RE structure, no trial_id
    beta = bam_fast(
      score_01 ~ deliberation_function +
        s(norm_mid, by = deliberation_function, k = 10) +
        s(log_n_chunks, k = 5) +
        s(subject_id, deliberation_function, bs = "re") +
        s(question,   deliberation_function, bs = "re"),
      betar(link = "logit"), d$active),

    # by-accuracy hurdle: both response random slopes plus trial_id
    hurdle_acc = bam_fast(
      active ~ deliberation_function * response +
        s(norm_mid, by = interaction(deliberation_function, response), k = 20) +
        s(log_n_chunks, k = 5) +
        s(subject_id, deliberation_function, bs = "re") +
        s(question,   deliberation_function, bs = "re") +
        s(subject_id, response, bs = "re") +
        s(question,   response, bs = "re") +
        s(trial_id,   bs = "re"),
      binomial(link = "logit"), d$long),

    # by-accuracy intensity: question response slope only, no trial_id
    beta_acc = bam_fast(
      score_01 ~ deliberation_function * response +
        s(norm_mid, by = interaction(deliberation_function, response), k = 10) +
        s(log_n_chunks, k = 5) +
        s(subject_id, deliberation_function, bs = "re") +
        s(question,   deliberation_function, bs = "re") +
        s(question,   response, bs = "re"),
      betar(link = "logit"), d$active),

    # lagged-confidence hurdles use three-level decomposition and trial_id
    hurdle_conf_n1 = bam_fast(
      active ~ deliberation_function * lag_conf_chunk_dev_1 +
        deliberation_function * conf_trial_dev +
        deliberation_function * conf_subject_mean +
        deliberation_function * lag_active_1 +
        s(norm_mid, by = deliberation_function, k = 10) +
        s(subject_id, deliberation_function, bs = "re") +
        s(question,   deliberation_function, bs = "re") +
        s(trial_id,   bs = "re"),
      binomial(link = "logit"), d$conf_n1),

    hurdle_conf_both = bam_fast(
      active ~ deliberation_function * lag_conf_chunk_dev_1 +
        deliberation_function * lag_conf_chunk_dev_2 +
        deliberation_function * conf_trial_dev +
        deliberation_function * conf_subject_mean +
        deliberation_function * lag_active_1 +
        deliberation_function * lag_active_2 +
        s(norm_mid, by = deliberation_function, k = 10) +
        s(subject_id, deliberation_function, bs = "re") +
        s(question,   deliberation_function, bs = "re") +
        s(trial_id,   bs = "re"),
      binomial(link = "logit"), d$conf_both),

    # lagged-confidence intensity: same decomposition, no trial_id
    beta_conf_n1 = bam_fast(
      score_01 ~ deliberation_function * lag_conf_chunk_dev_1 +
        deliberation_function * conf_trial_dev +
        deliberation_function * conf_subject_mean +
        deliberation_function * lag_score_01_1 +
        s(norm_mid, by = deliberation_function, k = 10) +
        s(subject_id, deliberation_function, bs = "re") +
        s(question,   deliberation_function, bs = "re"),
      betar(link = "logit"), d$active_conf_n1),

    beta_conf_both = bam_fast(
      score_01 ~ deliberation_function * lag_conf_chunk_dev_1 +
        deliberation_function * lag_conf_chunk_dev_2 +
        deliberation_function * conf_trial_dev +
        deliberation_function * conf_subject_mean +
        deliberation_function * lag_score_01_1 +
        deliberation_function * lag_score_01_2 +
        s(norm_mid, by = deliberation_function, k = 10) +
        s(subject_id, deliberation_function, bs = "re") +
        s(question,   deliberation_function, bs = "re"),
      betar(link = "logit"), d$active_conf_both),

    # lagged deliberation -> confidence: simple subject + question RE, no trial_id
    delib_n1 = bam_fast(
      confidence_01 ~ lag_confidence_1 +
        lag_control_chunk_dev_1       + control_trial_dev       + control_subject_mean +
        lag_generation_chunk_dev_1    + generation_trial_dev    + generation_subject_mean +
        lag_justification_chunk_dev_1 + justification_trial_dev + justification_subject_mean +
        lag_regulation_chunk_dev_1    + regulation_trial_dev    + regulation_subject_mean +
        s(norm_mid, k = 10) +
        s(subject_id, bs = "re") +
        s(question,   bs = "re"),
      betar(link = "logit"), d$delib_n1),

    delib_both = bam_fast(
      confidence_01 ~ lag_confidence_1 + lag_confidence_2 +
        lag_control_chunk_dev_1       + lag_control_chunk_dev_2       +
          control_trial_dev           + control_subject_mean +
        lag_generation_chunk_dev_1    + lag_generation_chunk_dev_2    +
          generation_trial_dev        + generation_subject_mean +
        lag_justification_chunk_dev_1 + lag_justification_chunk_dev_2 +
          justification_trial_dev     + justification_subject_mean +
        lag_regulation_chunk_dev_1    + lag_regulation_chunk_dev_2    +
          regulation_trial_dev        + regulation_subject_mean +
        s(norm_mid, k = 10) +
        s(subject_id, bs = "re") +
        s(question,   bs = "re"),
      betar(link = "logit"), d$delib_both)
  )
}
```

#### Trajectory models

```{r chunk-110 }
# response-scale curves for one fitted model along norm_mid, via get_itsadug_curve
# to match the main-analysis prediction pipeline (rm.ranef + sim.ci)
curves_norm_mid <- function(model, data, by_response = FALSE) {
  grid_mid   <- seq(0, 1, length.out = 200)
  log_nc_ref <- median(data$log_n_chunks, na.rm = TRUE)
  funcs      <- levels(data$deliberation_function)

  build <- function(func, resp = NA_character_) {
    cond <- list(norm_mid              = grid_mid,
                 deliberation_function = func,
                 log_n_chunks          = log_nc_ref,
                 subject_id            = data$subject_id[1],
                 question              = data$question[1],
                 trial_id              = data$trial_id[1])
    keep <- "deliberation_function"
    if (!is.na(resp)) {
      cond$response <- resp
      keep <- c(keep, "response")
    }
    get_itsadug_curve(model, cond = cond, keep = keep)
  }

  if (by_response) {
    crossing(func = funcs, resp = levels(data$response)) %>%
      pmap_dfr(build)
  } else {
    map_dfr(funcs, build)
  }
}

# data slot to predict from depends on whether the model used active-only data
data_for <- list(hurdle = "long", beta = "active",
                 hurdle_acc = "long", beta_acc = "active")

# pull predictions for one model family across scenarios
traj_curves <- function(model_name, by_response = FALSE) {
  slot <- data_for[[model_name]]
  robustness_fits %>%
    mutate(curves = map(fit,
                        ~ curves_norm_mid(.x[[model_name]], .x$data[[slot]],
                                          by_response = by_response))) %>%
    select(label, curves) %>%
    unnest(curves) %>%
    mutate(scenario = factor(label, levels = scenario_levels))
}
```

```{r chunk-111 }
plot_overall_traj <- function(curves_df, y_lab, title) {
  ggplot(curves_df, aes(x = norm_mid, y = .fitted,
                        color = deliberation_function,
                        fill  = deliberation_function)) +
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = .lower_ci, ymax = .upper_ci),
                alpha = 0.15, color = NA) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
    facet_wrap(~ scenario, ncol = length(scenario_levels),
               labeller = as_labeller(scenario_labels)) +
    scale_color_manual(values = function_colors,
                       breaks = names(function_colors)[1:4]) +
    scale_fill_manual(values  = function_colors,
                      breaks = names(function_colors)[1:4]) +
    labs(x = "Relative time", y = y_lab,
         color = "Deliberation function", fill = "Deliberation function") +
    guides(color = guide_legend(title.position = "top", title.hjust = 0.5)) +
    jtools::theme_apa(legend.use.title = TRUE) +
    theme(legend.position = "top",
          legend.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
          plot.title = element_blank(),
          plot.subtitle = element_blank())
}
```

##### Correct − Incorrect difference curves

```{r chunk-115 }
# difference curves on the link scale via itsadug::get_difference, faceted by scenario
diff_curves <- function(model_name) {
  grid <- seq(0, 1, length.out = 200)
  robustness_fits %>%
    mutate(diffs = map(fit, function(f) {
      data <- f$data$long
      map_dfr(levels(data$deliberation_function), function(fn) {
        get_difference(
          f[[model_name]],
          comp    = list(response = c("Correct", "Incorrect")),
          cond    = list(deliberation_function = fn, norm_mid = grid),
          rm.ranef = TRUE, sim.ci = TRUE, print.summary = FALSE
        ) %>%
          as_tibble() %>%
          mutate(deliberation_function = fn)
      })
    })) %>%
    select(label, diffs) %>%
    unnest(diffs) %>%
    mutate(scenario              = factor(label, levels = scenario_levels),
           deliberation_function = factor(deliberation_function,
                                          levels = names(function_colors)))
}

# significant segments for facet_grid(deliberation_function ~ scenario).
# significance bands sit on the x axis, at the same height across panels.
plot_diff <- function(diff_df, y_lab, title) {

  global_y_min <- min(diff_df$difference - diff_df$CI)
  global_y_max <- max(diff_df$difference + diff_df$CI)

  sig_df <- diff_df %>%
    mutate(sig = (difference - CI) > 0 | (difference + CI) < 0) %>%
    group_by(scenario, deliberation_function) %>%
    mutate(block = cumsum(sig != lag(sig, default = first(sig)))) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    filter(sig) %>%
    group_by(scenario, deliberation_function, block) %>%
    summarise(x = min(norm_mid), xend = max(norm_mid), .groups = "drop") %>%
    # place segments right on top of the x axis
    mutate(y_sig = global_y_min)

  ggplot(diff_df, aes(x = norm_mid, y = difference)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = difference - CI, ymax = difference + CI),
                alpha = 0.3, fill = "grey60") +
    geom_line(color = "black", linewidth = 1) +
    geom_segment(data = sig_df,
                 aes(x = x, xend = xend, y = y_sig, yend = y_sig),
                 inherit.aes = FALSE, color = "black", linewidth = 1.8) +
    facet_grid(deliberation_function ~ scenario,
               labeller = labeller(scenario = scenario_labels)) +
    scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))) +
    labs(x = "Relative time", y = y_lab) +
    jtools::theme_apa() +
    theme(
      strip.text.y  = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12),
      strip.text.x  = element_text(size = 10),
      panel.spacing = unit(1.0, "lines"),
      plot.title    = element_blank(),
      plot.subtitle = element_blank()
    )
}
```
